Between 14-25 August, 2006 the 26th General Assembly of the International Astronomical Union was held in Prague (Czech Republic). The assembly excluded Pluto from the list of planets and reclassified it as a dwarf planet.
Planets differ from each other depending on their size, composition, temperature and time taken for a revolution. The main reason for this difference is their
distance
from the sun.
Some planets like Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars are solid; these planets are called
terrestrial planets
whereas some planets have a gaseous composition like Jupiter and Saturn. Due to their large size these planets are also known as
Jovian Planets
(Jovian means like Jupiter).
Out of all the 8 planets, Earth has the maximum mean density i.e. 5.5 g/cm³. The mean density of other planets is as follows –
Mercury (5.4 g/cm³), Venus (5.2 g/cm³), Mars (3.9 g/cm³), Jupiter (1.3 g/cm³), Saturn (0.7 g/cm³), Uranus (1.3 g/cm³), Neptune (1.6 g/cm³).
The Sun alone carries 99.8% of the total mass of the solar system.
Sun’s mass is 1.989 × 10³⁰ kilograms which is
times that of the planet Earth.
Mercury is the
smallest planet
of the solar system whereas Jupiter is the
largest
Venus is the
brightest planet
whereas
Neptune
is the farthest. Neptune takes the maximum time in to complete one revolution around the Sun (165 yrs).
The descending order of
planets according to their size
is as follows - Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune, Earth, Venus, Mars, Mercury.
The descending order of the
planets according to their mass
is as follows – Jupiter, Saturn, Neptune, Uranus, Earth, Venus, Mars & Mercury.
The ascending order of
planets according to their distance from the Sun
is as follows
– Mercury, Venus, Earth, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, Uranus, Neptune.
Among all the planets, Jupiter has the
maximum gravitational acceleration

Gases like hydrogen and helium are found in abundance on planets like Jupiter and Saturn. The Goldilocks zone is also called the habitable zone. In astronomy, the Goldilocks zone is the range of the orbits around a star within which a planetary surface can support liquid water given sufficient atmospheric pressure. Liquid water is one of the most important elements in finding life on other planets. Earth is the only known life-supporting planet in the solar system, and it lies in the Sun's Goldilocks zone. This zone is neither too hot nor too cold.
By 1514, Polish astronomer and mathematician
Ncolaus Copernicus

had written the handwritten essay 'Commentariolus' (Little Commentary). In this essay, he gave information regarding the principle of revolution. According to this essay, the Sun is at the center of the universe and earth revolves around it. Later in 1543 AD, it was been published by the name 'De revolutionibus orbium coelestium (On the Revolutions of the Heavenly Spheres).
It is noteworthy to mention that in 6th century A.D. i.e. 1000 years before Nicolaus Copernicus. The famous Indian astronomer
Varamihira
had already proposed the theory that, the Moon revolves around the Earth and Earth revolves around the Sun.
Johannes Kepler
was a German astronomer, mathematician and astrologer. He is best known for propounding the ‘three laws of planetary motion’.
Galileo Galilei
, the famous scientist of Italy gave us the fundamental principles of falling bodies.
English scientist
Isaac Newton
gave us the fundamental principles of velocity and also discovered the laws of gravity.
The sun is the centre of our solar system. The bright outer layer that emits most of the radiation, particularly the visible light is known as the
Photosphere
According to NASA the diameter of the sun is

times bigger than our planet earth. The mean radius of the sun is 695700 km. Due to the very high temperature in the sun’s core (appx. 15,000,000 oC) every matter present in it is either in a gaseous state or in the
plasma state
Plasma is the 4th state of matter after solid, liquid and gas. As per NASA, the surface temperature of the sun is
. The entire source of the Sun’s energy is a result of
nuclear fusion
- the fusing of hydrogen into helium, creating energy.
Nuclear reactions are of two types-
nuclear fusion
and
nuclear fission
In
nuclear fusion
, two or more atomic nuclei are combined to form one or more different atomic nuclei and subatomic particles (neutrons or protons).
Nuclear fission

is a reaction in which a heavy nucleus splits spontaneously or on impact with another particle, with the release of energy. The release of energy from the stars is due to nuclear fusion. In stars when the temperature reaches between 1 to 1.5 crore Celsius. The atoms of hydrogen fuse together to form helium.
H2 + H2 He4 + Energy
Deuterium Helium
Solar eclipse
is a situation when the complete or partial hiding of the sun is caused by the moon’s passing between the sun and the earth. A solar eclipse occurs only on a
new moon day
. The outer layer of the sun which is visible during a solar eclipse is known as the
corona.
In any circumstances, the maximum duration of a total solar eclipse cannot exceed
7.5 minutes

When a solar flare enters the atmosphere of our planet, they collide with the air particles and produces a beautiful display of a light show especially in the regions of upper latitude. This display is known as
Aurora lights
. At North Pole it is called
Aurora Borealis
and at the South Pole, it is called
Aurora Australis
A dark patch on the surface of the sun is known as a
sunspot
. Sunspots appear as regions with temperature about 1500K cooler than the surrounding photospheres.
We can often witness a white color ring around the sun and the moon, it is known as a
halo

. It is caused when the light gets refracted or reflected due to the presence of cirrus and cirrostratus clouds in the upper layers of the atmosphere. The distance between the sun and the earth is minimum in the first week of January, this situation or position is called
'Perihelion'
. Generally Perihelion occurs on 4th January. While opposite to it is on 4th July, the sun stands farthest from the earth and this position or situation is known as
'Aphelion'

Astronomical unit is used for measuring distance or length. For general reference, we can say that one Astronomical unit represents the mean distance between the earth and the sun (149.598 ×10⁶ km or 149.6×10⁶ km). In meters it is 149.59 × 10⁹; In millimetres it is 149.59 × 10¹².
It is the smallest planet of the solar system and is nearest to the sun. It completes its one revolution in around 88 days.
Mercury and Venus are the planets having no satellites.
The absence of atmosphere makes it impossible for the sustenance of any life on Mercury.
The average range of temperature on Mercury is around
Mariner 10

was a satellite launched by NASA that traveled very close to Mercury and took photos of the planet. From the pictures, it was found that the surface of the planet Mercury has a number of mountains and plains. The distance between the Sun and Mercury is approx. 57.9 million km or 0.39 AU.

All the 8 planets of the solar system revolve around the sun. The time taken for one revolution around the sun, by every planet is as follows – Mercury (88 days), Venus (224.7 days), Earth (365.2 days), Mars (687 days), Jupiter (11.86 years), Saturn (29.4 yrs), Uranus (84.07 yrs), Neptune (164.9 yrs).
Albedo
is an expression of the ability of surfaces to reflect sunlight (heat from the Sun).
Light coloured surfaces return a large part of the sun’s rays back to space (high albedo). Dark surfaces absorb the rays from the sun (low albedo). Hence, Albedo determines the brightness of a body.
Mercury receives a very high amount of sunlight but its albedo is low as compared to earth hence the planet Mercury is not that bright in nature.
The albedo of Earth is 0.3 whereas the albedo of Mercury is mere 0.1. The diameter of planet Mercury is appx. 4879 km.
Venus is also known as the
twin sister
of planet Earth. Venus is the
brightest planet
as seen from Earth, in night sky. It is also known as the
Morning Star
and
Evening Star

. The average distance from the Sun is appx 108.2 million km. It is the second closest planet to our sun. It takes Venus appx. 225 (224.7) days to complete its one revolution. It is the hottest planet in the solar system with an average temperature of 464°C (737K).
The temperature of the planets in the solar system is as follows –
Every planet in our solar system except for Venus and Uranus rotates
clockwise
i.e., from east to west.

Venus has a thick atmosphere. The atmosphere of Venus mainly comprises of carbon-dioxide (about 96.5%), with average temperatures increasing above 400°C. That is why the planet experiences a pressure cooker like condition. Hence because of the above conditions sustenance of any life form becomes next to impossible on this planet.
Just like Mercury & Venus too has
no natural satellite
of its own.
In the year 1989
Magellan spacecraft
was sent to Venus on a deep space mission for the next 4 years i.e., from 1990-1994. It observed the planet Venus and its features. The satellite was named after
Ferdinand Magellan
, a famous Portuguese explorer of the 16th century.

The Earth is the third planet from the sun behind Mercury and Venus respectively. It is located between Venus and Mars. Survival of life is possible on our planet because of its ecology. Hence Earth has been given the name Green Planet.

Greek Philosopher Aristotle (384-322 B.C.) has clearly mentioned in second volume of the 14th chapter of his book "On The Heavens". But now it is universally accepted that the shape of our planet is much closer to being an
oblate spheroid
. Hence, the shape of our planet is called Geoid (Geoid meaning earth like).
Our planet Earth is tilted on its axis at an angle of
The Earth takes 24 hours to rotate once on its axis. This leads to the phenomena of Day and Night.
Basically that part of the planet which is facing the sun experiences day and the opposite side experiences night.
The axial tilt of 23⁰30' (now 23⁰44') as it moves around the Sun causes seasonal changes.
The
moon
is an astronomical body that orbits planet Earth and is Earth’s only permanent natural satellite.

On 21st March and 23rd September the Sun shines directly above the equator twice. From 21st March to 23rd September (6 months) the Sun shines between the equator and tropic of cancer. Thus, the Northern Hemisphere experiences summers and the Southern Hemisphere experiences winters.

On the other hand, the next 6 months i.e. from 23rd September to 21st of March the sun shines between the equator and the tropic of Capricorn. Hence, the southern hemisphere experiences summers and the northern hemisphere experiences winters.

Because of the slanted rays falling on the hemisphere, opposite to the one receiving direct sunlight, at any point north of the Arctic Circle or south of the Antarctic Circle there will be one period in the summer when the sun does not set, and one period in winter when the sun does not rise. For example in Northern Hemisphere the sun does not set at the North Pole and vice-versa.
On June 21st, the sun is directly overhead the Tropic of Cancer. This phenomenon is known as the
Summer Solstice
. On 22nd December, the sun is directly overhead the Tropic of Capricorn. This phenomenon is called the
Winter Solstice
The 45-degree latitude is often called the halfway point between the equator and the North Pole. The cosine 45 latitude equals to 0.707, hence the length of this latitude is

0.707 × 40090.2857 = 28343.832 km. Therefore, the length of the 45° latitude is more than half of the length of the equator. The length of 60-degree latitude is half the length of the equator (cosine 60° = 0.5). The circumference of the equator is appx. 40090 km. Whereas the equatorial diameter of the Earth is appx. 12800 (12756 km).
The rotation of the Earth creates a
centrifugal force
which is
maximum at the equator
. As a result of this force, the weight of any object is minimum at the equator and increases with an increase in latitudes and is maximum at the poles.
The movement of the Earth in its orbit around the sun is called a revolution. It takes Earth
365.25 Days
or
365 Days
hours 9 minutes and
seconds to complete one revolution.
A
tropical year

(also known as a solar year) is the time that the Sun takes to return to the same position in the cycles of the seasons, as seen from Earth; for example, the time from the Vernal equinox to Vernal equinox or from summer solstice to summer solstice.
The one tropical year is approx. 365.24 days. Normally a calendar is based on a tropical year, which is 365 days, 5 hours, 48 min. and 45.2 seconds long.
The year 2000 AD witnessed an increase of 5 minutes in the length of the year. The length of the year was 365 days, 6 hours, 13 min. and 53.26 seconds. These types of years are called
Anomalistic years
The Earth revolves around the Sun at an average speed of
km/sec (appx. 30km/sec). The revolution speed of the other planets in the solar system is as follows – (1) Mercury 47.4 km/s, (2) Venus – 35 km/s, (3) Earth – 29.78 km/s (4) Mars – 24.1 km/s
(5) Jupiter – 13.1 km/s, (6) Saturn – 9.7 km/s (7) Uranus – 6.8 km/s (8) Neptune – 5.4 km/s.
The average distance between the sun and the Earth is 149597870.7 km. It takes appx.
min. and

seconds for the Sun’s rays to reach our planet. These electromagnetic energy waves travel at a speed of186282 miles/sec. The closest star to Earth is the Sun. The distance of other stars from our planet Earth is as follows– (1) Alpha Centauri - 4.35 light years, (2) Sun – 149.6 × 10⁶ km, (3) Sirius A (Dog Star) – 8.6 light years.
The Earth’s magnetic field varies from place to place. Thumba is an ideal location for satellites as a result, The
Thumba Equatorial Rocket Launching Station
was established here.
Thumba is located in Thiruvananthapuram, the district of Kerala.

The projection of maximum artificial satellites is towards the east of the planet Earth. This is because a satellite launched towards the east direction will get an initial boost equal to the velocity of the earth surface. Thus, the initial boost helps in cutting down the cost of rockets used to launch the satellite. However, a satellite is not always projected towards the east. Such satellites that are to be placed in polar orbits are launched in the south or north directions.
The inner core of our planet is solid. The outer core is in liquid form. The core has a depth of 2900 km.
The crust is composed of different elements in varied proportions. They are as follows (according to percentage by weight) -
Oxygen
Silicon
Aluminium
Iron
Calcium
Sodium
Potassium
Magnesium
Earth Day
is an annual event celebrated on
April 22
worldwide. It was first observed in the year 1970.
Mars is the fourth planet from the sun third being Earth.
The axial tilt of Mars is 25°12' relative to its orbital plane.

Mars average distance from the Sun is roughly 227943824 km (228 million km) and its orbital period is 687.0 Earth days. The diameter of Mars is 6792 km and it takes 24.7 hours to complete one rotation.
The atmospheric composition of Mars is CO₂- 95.1%, N₂-2.59%, Argon - 1.94%, Oxygen -
0.16% and traces of water.
NASA's
Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter
(MRO), took pictures of Mars with the help of its hi tech cameras. After studying the pictures, scientists were able to claim the presence of liquid water on Mars.
The MRO contains a host of scientific instruments such as imaging spectrometers that helped in finding the hydrated minerals of the planet. The average temperature of Mars, it is – 65°C (208 K).
Mars and Earth are very different planets when it comes to temperature, size and atmosphere, but original processes on the two Planets are surprisingly similar.
Mars is often referred to as the
Red planet
because the reddish iron oxide prevalent on its surface gives it a reddish appearance.
Mars has two relatively small natural moons,
Phobos
and
Deimos
The Olympus Mons (formerly Nix Olympica) mountain (volcano) of Mars is approx. three times the size of our Mount Everest.
The
Phoenix Mars Lander

was a space exploration mission of NASA on Mars under the Scout program. It was launched on August 4th, 2007 and landed on Mars on May 25th, 2008. The mission was declared concluded on November 2, 2008. Phoenix was the first lander that gave valuable inputs regarding the
presence of ice
on the planet.
The
Curiosity Rover
was launched by NASA to explore the possibility of life, determine the role of water, and study the climate and geology of Mars. The Mars Orbiter Mission (MOM) or
Mangalyaan

is India’s first Mars exploration mission. It was launched on 5th November 2013 by the Indian Space Research Organization (ISRO). It was launched with the help of the PSLV- C25 rocket. It was inserted into Mars’s orbit on 24 September 2014. Now, with the success of the MoM mission India has become a member of the elite Mars club (United States of America, Russia, European Union).
Jupiter is the fifth planet from the Sun and the largest in the solar system. Its diameter is 142984 km. The average density of Jupiter is 1326 kg/m³.
The descending order of planets in the solar system as per their diameter is as follows
– Jupiter (142984 km), Saturn (120536 km),, Uranus (51118 km), Neptune (49528 km), Earth (12756km), Venus (12104 km), Mars (6792 km), Mercury (4879 km).
It takes Jupiter
11.86 years to complete one revolution around the sun.
As of 27 January 2026, 97 satellites of Jupiter have been discovered. Among these, the 4 largest satellites of Jupiter are
Io
Europa
Ganymede
and
Callisto
. These four are also known as Galilean Moons. They were first seen by Galileo Galilei in January 1610 and recognized by him as satellites of Jupiter.
Ganymede

is the largest and most massive moon of Jupiter and in the solar system. Jupiter is also known as miniature solar system. Voyager-1 spacecraft was sent to explore the Jovian system in 1977. It explored Europa (one of the four Galilean moons). It provided detailed images of Europa’s icy surface. Hence causing many scientists to speculate about the possibility of a liquid ocean similar to those found on Earth. These liquid oceans possibly have a depth of appx. 60-150 km.
If it is proven then Europa will be the only place in the solar system apart from our planet Earth where water is present in that quantity.
Jupiter’s ring
was first discovered by the
Voyager 1
spacecraft in 1979. These rings are also known as
Jovian Rings

. These rings are mostly made of silicate and dust particles. It is because of the transparency that these rings are difficult to spot however their existence cannot be questioned. Jupiter is primarily composed of hydrogen and helium. Some traces of methane, ammonia hydrogen deuteride, ethanel etc. is are also found. Jupiter is the fastest spinning planet in the solar system.
Saturn is the sixth planet from the sun and the second largest in the solar system. It has
natural satellites.
Titan
is its largest satellite, having a diameter of 5150 km.
Rhea
is the second largest natural satellite of Saturn having a diameter of 1528 km.
Other natural satellites of Saturn include Dione, Tethys, Mimas, Enceladus, Lapetus, Helene, Atlas, etc. It takes Saturn about 29.4 years to finish one revolution around the sun.
Saturn is also known as
‘Globe of Gases’
and
‘Galaxy Like Planet’
Saturn is probably best known for the system of planetary rings that make it visually unique. Planetary rings A,B,D and E of the planet Saturn are visible from Earth.
The most prominent and most famous planetary rings in the solar system are those around Saturn, but the other three giant planets Jupiter, Uranus, and Neptune also have a ring system.

Saturn appears to the naked eye in the night sky as a bright, yellowish point of light. The duration of a day on Saturn is 10 hours 34 minutes and the planet's axial tilt is 26°70'. The average surface temperature of Saturn is –140°C.
The atmosphere of Saturn contains, hydrogen and helium. Trace amounts of methane, hydrogen Deuteride, ethane etc. Ammonia has also been detected in saturns atmosphere.
The magnetic field of saturn's is 578 times as powerful that of our planet Earth. The Phoebe satellite of Saturn orbits Saturn opposite to Saturn’s rotation.
The Cassini probe was sent on 15th October, 1997 to orbit the planet Saturn.

chapters.title: The Universe · The Uranus, Neptune and Pluto

runs: Uranus is the 7th planet from the Sun and the third largest planet in the solar system. Uranus was discovered by Sir William Herschel on 13th March 1781. The axial tilt or equatorial inclination of Uranus is 97.77°. Like Venus, Uranus rotates east to west. Uranus takes about 17 hours and 14 minutes to rotate on its axis, and about 84 Earth years to complete an orbit of the Sun (a Uranian year).
On Uranus, the Sun rises in the west and sets in the east.
The composition of Uranus atmosphere is different from its bulk, consisting mainly of molecular hydrogen, helium, methane and ammonia etc..
Due to its distance from the Sun, Uranus is an
ice giant
and appears to be blue-green in colour due to presence of methane in its atmosphere. Uranus has 29 (as of March, 2025) moons. Just like Saturn, Uranus also has planetary rings.

Neptune was discovered by German astronomer Johann Gottfried Galle on the night of 23-24 September 1846. One day on Neptune takes about 16 hours and 6 minutes (the time it takes for Neptune to rotate), and Neptune makes a complete orbit around the sun in about 164.9 years. Neptune’s axis of rotation is tilted at
with respect to the plane of its orbit around the sun.
Neptune is the
coldest planet
in the solar system with an average temperature of-200°C. Neptune does not have a solid surface. Its atmosphere is mostly made up of hydrogen, helium and methane.
Neptune has 16 known natural satellites among these
Triton
and
Nereid
are the prominent one.
In 2006 when Pluto was excluded from the category of planets, Neptune became the farthest planet in the solar system.
Pluto was discovered by Clyde Tombaugh in 1930. It was considered to be the smallest and the 9th planet of the solar system.
Between 14 to 25 August 2006, the 26th General Assembly of the International Astronomical Union was held in
Prague
(Czech Republic). The assembly excluded Pluto from the list of planets and reclassified it as a dwarf planet. This was because the orbit of Pluto was overlapping with that of Neptune.
Pluto has five known natural satellites. The closest to Pluto is
Charon
, followed by
Styx
Nix
Kerberos
and
Hydra
. Charon is the largest natural 'satellite' of Pluto. Pluto takes about 247.9 years to complete one revolution around the sun.
The moon is an astronomical body that orbits planet Earth and is Earth’s only permanent natural satellite. The diameter of the Moon is 3,475 km.
The minimum and maximum distance between the Earth and Moon is
km and
km respectively.
The Moon makes a complete orbit around Earth once every
days,
hours and

minutes. It is the same time that is taken by the Moon to complete its one rotation. The moon is tilted on its axis, due to which its appearance (size) changes with its distance from the Earth. Because of this effect, about 59% of the Moon’s surface can actually be seen from Earth.
Sound requires a medium to travel. Since there is
no atmosphere
on the Moon, When two astronomers talk to each other it is not audible.
Solar eclipses
occur at the new moon, when the moon comes in between the sun and the earth. In contrast,
lunar eclipses
occur at full moon, when the earth is in between the sun and the moon. The type and duration of a lunar eclipse depend upon the orbital tilt and alignment of the moon.
When the moon is closest to Earth (363300 km), then this condition is called
perigee
. It is during this time that
high tides
occur, because the gravitational pull of the moon is at its maximum. When the moon is at its farthest distance from the earth, the condition is called
apogee
. This is the time when low tides occur because the gravitational pull of the Moon is minimum.
The low tides are
smaller than the high tides.

A lunar perigee occurred on December 22nd, 1999 due to which the moon appeared to be the brightest. Again on November 14th, 2016 a full perigee occurred due to which the moon for the first time in over 60 years appeared to be the largest and the brightest. In common language, this phenomenon is known as
supermoon
. A supermoon occurs when the full moon coincides with the moon's orbit being closest (perigee) to Earth.
During a supermoon, the moon appears roughly 14%, larger in diameter and 30% brighter.

During a total lunar eclipse, earth completely blocks direct sunlight from reaching the moon. The only light reflected from the lunar surface has been refracted by Earth’s Atmosphere. Due to the reddish colour, a totally eclipsed moon is sometimes called a
blood moon
A
Blue Moon

is an additional full moon that appears in a subdivision of a year-either as the third or fourth full moon in a season or a second full moon in a month of the common calendar. One lunar month is around
29.5 days

long. Ifwe multiply 29.5 days by 12 months we get 354 days, which means there could be 12 full moons in a year. Since 11 days are still left in a year, approximately every 2.7154 years the condition for a Blue moon (one extra full moon) comes into existence. In every 2.7154 years there would be a month that has two full moons, however the difference between these two full moons will always be
days. Traditionally the
second full moon of the month
is called a Blue Moon.
Accordingly in the year 2009 there were two full moons in December, one on 2nd December and one on 31st December. The one that occurred on 31st December was called a Blue Moon.

According to the new definition of the Almanac the Blue Moon phenomenon is the occurrence of one extra full moon in an astronomical season. There are four astronomical seasons in a year- starting from 21st March to 23rd September (the Equinoxes) and the other two starting from 21st June to 22nd December (summer and winter solstice respectively). Hence the astronomical seasons are like this –
1st Astronomical season (21st March to 20th June)

2nd Astronomical season (21st June to 22nd September) 3rd Astronomical season (23rd September to 21st December) 4th Astronomical season (22nd December to 20th March) Every season is divided into 3 months. Hence every season will normally have 3 full moons, however in every 2.7154 years, one of the above 4 seasons will have 4 full moons instead of3. The astronomical season that has the 4th full moon will be known as the season with the Blue Moon. It is to be noted however that the
3rd full moon will be considered as the Blue moon

and not the 4th one. It is because only then will the names of the other full moons, such as the moon before the solstice and the Moon after the solstice, fall at the proper times relative to the solstices and equinoxes. Hence, according to the above definition, the year 2010 witnessed 4 full moons the astronomical season starting from 23rd September to 22nd December. 25th September, 24th October, 21st November and 20th December witnessed full moons. The full moon of21st November 2010 was referred to as a Blue Moon.

The weight of any body on a planet or satellite depends upon the mass of the body and the gravitational acceleration of the planet. (Weight = mass × gravitational acceleration). The gravitational acceleration on the moon is
1/6th

of that of planet Earth. Hence, any body or object taken to the moon has its weight reduced to 1/6th of its weight on planet Earth. The area of the large black patch as seen from the Earth is called Lunar Mare or
Sea of Tranquility
. It was the landing site for the first crewed landing on the Moon on July 20, 1969. Astronauts
Neil Armstrong
and Edwin
Buzz Aldrin Junior
made a smooth touchdown in the Apollo 11 Lunar Module named Eagle. The third astronaut on this mission was
Michael Collins
, however, he did not step on the Moon.

The Apollo 11 returned to Earth and splashed down in the Pacific Ocean on July 24, 1969. The mission brought back substances from the surface of the Moon which weighed around 47 pounds. It was used for research purposes.
Chandrayaan-1

was India’s first lunar probe. It was launched by the Indian Space Research Organisation on 22 October, 2008 and operated until August 2009. India launched the space craft using a PSLV-XL rocket (PSLV-C11). The vehicle was inserted into lunar orbit on 8 November 2008.
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) set up a Indian Deep Space Network (IDSN) centre in Byalalu (Bengaluru) to track Chandrayaan-1.
Chandrayaan-2

is India’s second lunar exploration mission after Chandrayaan-1 developed by the Indian Space Research Organisation, the mission was launched to the Moon by a Geosynchronous Satellite Launch Vehicle Mk III - M1 (GSLV-MkIII-M1) on July 22, 2019. Chandrayaan-3 mission took off on July 14, 2023 from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Andhra Pradesh. On August 5, 2023 the mission entered lunar orbit. On August 17, the lander module separated from the propulsion module. The first and second deboosting occurred on August 18 and 20 respectively. OnAugust 23, 2023 the lander landed on the south pole of the Moon. India's third lunar mission, Chandrayaan - 3 made history in August, 2023 by successfully achieving a soft landing on the south pole of the Moon.
With this, India became the first nation to land on the Moon's south pole and the fourth (after Russia, U.S.A. and China) to land successfully on Earth's only natural satellite.
The group of small pieces of rock and metal revolving around the Sun between the orbits of Mars and Jupiter is called asteroids.
Asteroids, vary in size and some can be
in diameter for example Ceres.
According to the position of these asteroids in space, they are categorized in the following way –
Main belt
- In this belt, there are some prominent asteroids named Hungaria, Flora, Phocaea, Eos, Themis, Cybele, Hilda and Koronis.
(ii)
Near Earth Asteroids (NEAs)
- Among these Aten, Apollo, Amor and Atira are prominent ones.
(iii)
Trojans
- Near the Lagrange point of the planet Jupiter orbit.

chapters.title: The Universe · The Comets and Meteors

runs: A comet is an icy, small solar system body that, when pass ing close to the sun, warms and begins to release gases. This produces a visible atmosphere or coma and sometimes also a tail. Comets usually have highly elliptical orbits and they revolve around the sun. Sometimes the tail of these comets can be millions of kilometers long.
Comets generally have two kinds of tails – (1) comprised of dust particles and (2) ionized. Both are generated from the Coma.
The Sun's radiation pressure and solar wind accelerate materials away from the comet’s head at different velocities according to the size and mass of the materials.
Halley's

Comet was last seen in Earth's skies in 1986 and will return in 2061 on its regular 76 year journey around the Sun. The Halley is a short period comet. On 23rd July 1995, the Hale-Bopp comet was first seen near Jupiter. It was discovered by Alan Hale (New Mexico) and
Thomas Bopp
(Arizona). The last names of these two people were combined to name this comet. The Hale-Bopp is a long period comet which takes 2534 years to revolve around the Sun.
The Hale-Bopp comet is 1000 times brighter than the Halley comet, even though they are at the same distances. The comet
Shoemaker Levy-9

was discovered on 24th March, 1993 by astronomers Eugene M. Shoemaker, Carolyn Shoemaker and David Levy. The last names of both the astronomers were used to name the comet. Between 16 and 22 July 1994, the comet collided with Jupiter, providing the first direct observation of an extraterrestrial collision of solar system objects. However, Jupiter was not harmed by this collision.
67 P/Churyumov-Gerasimenko was the destination of the
Rosetta mission
launched on 2nd March 2004. It was the first mission to land a
spacecraft on a comet
. It was launched from the Guiana Space Centre in French Guiana on an Ariane 5G+ rocket and reached comet Churyumov-Gerasimenko on 6 August 2014.
i. Latitudes
Latitude is the angular distance of a point on the earth’s surface, measured in degrees from the center of the earth.
It is parallel to the line of the equator, which lies midway between the poles.
The latitude angle is denoted by the Greek lowercase letter Phi (). 0° latitude is also known as the
equato
r. It is halfway between the North Pole and the South Pole. The equator thus divides the planet into the Northern and Southern hemisphere.
The earth is widest at the equator. All other latitudes are smaller than the equator.

The North Pole has a latitude of 90°N and the South Pole has a latitude of 90°S. In each hemisphere, latitudes are counted from 0° to the poles. Hence, altogether there are 179 latitudes (including the equator). Besides this, there are 179 real circle latitudes as the 90° N and 90°S latitudes are points on the earth’s surface.
The 23.5° N latitude in the Northern Hemisphere is known as the
Tropic of Cancer
whereas the 66.5° N latitude in the Northern Hemisphere is known as
Arctic Circle
Similarly, the 23.5°S latitude in the southern Hemisphere is known as the
Tropic of Capricorn
and 66.5° south latitude in the Southern Hemisphere is known as the
Antarctic Circle.

The 0° latitude (equator) and 0° longitude (Prime Meridian) intersect each other in the Gulf of Guinea located on the western coast of Africa. The Gulf is located in the Atlantic Ocean. The north and south of any place on a globe or a map is determined by latitudes. The latitudinal value in degrees of any place is directly proportional to its extent in the north of the equator for example - Beijing (China) - 39°55'N, New Delhi - 28°38'N, New York (USA) - 40°45' N and Rome (Italy) - 41°54' N. Hence among these Rome is the most northern city.
Longitudes are imaginary lines joining the North and South Poles. They are also known as Meridians of Longitude or Lines of Longitude.

By convention, one of the longitudes was called the Prime Meridian. The longitudes of other places are measured as the angle east or west from the Prime Meridian, ranging from 0° at the Prime Meridian, to 180° eastward and 180° westward. In 1884, at the International Meridian Conference in Washington, D.C., 22 countries voted to adopt the
Greenwich meridian

as the Prime Meridian of the world. The 180th Meridian or Antemeridian is the meridian 180° both east and west of the Prime Meridian. Thus, it is common to both east longitude and west longitude. Hence there are 360 longitudes.
Since Earth makes one complete rotation of 360° in one day or
24 hours
, it passes through 15° in one hour or 1° in 4 minutes. The Earth rotates from west to east, so every 15° we go eastward local time is advanced by 1 hour.

The International Date Line, established in 1884 passes through the Mid-Pacific Ocean and roughly follows a 180° longitude North-South line on the Earth. It is located halfway around the world from the prime meridian.

When we cross the International Date Line from west to east, there is a decrease of one day and if you cross the line from east to west there is a gain of an extra day. This is because there is a difference of 24 hours between 180°E and 180°W longitude. 180°E and 180°W longitude are the same and written as only 180°.
The time at 180°E is 12 hours ahead and at 180° W it is 12 hours behind Greenwich time. A time zone is a region or area that observes the same standard time. The 360 longitudes have been divided into
24 time zones
. The world is divided longitudinally into time zones, with each hour difference roughly
apart. This means that every time zone has a difference of 1 hour and every longitude has a difference of 4 minutes.
The international standard time is determined by the prime meridian.
In the Northern Hemisphere the Prime Meridian passes through the
United Kingdom
France
and
Spain
in
Europe
and
Algeria
Mali
Burkina Faso
Togo
and
Ghana
in
Africa
. The only landmass crossed by the Meridian in the Southern Hemisphere is
Antarctica

Apart from the United Kingdom there are a few more countries that despite being away from GMT (Greenwich Mean Time), use it for determining their standard time. These countries/areas are – Iceland, Ireland, Portugal, Western Sahara, Sao Tome Mauritania, Mali, Senegal, Guinea-Bissau, Guinea, Ghana, Liberia, Cote d'Ivoire, Burkina Faso, Gambia, Saint Helena etc. The time difference between Indian Standard Time (82°30' E longitude) and GMT is
5.30 hours
Katchal

, a tiny island near Nicobar Island was virtually unknown untill the Royal Greenwich Laboratory declared that it would be the first inhabited place on Earth to catch the rays of the first sunrise of the millennium. The
Katchal
island is located at a distance of 1600 km from the mainland of India and 418 km from Port Blair port. The island is located at 7°56' North latitude and 93° 24' East longitude.
International Date Line
(IDL) is an imaginary line of demarcation on the surface of the Earth that runs from the North Pole to the South Pole and demarcates the change of one calendar day to the next.

IDL is roughly based on the meridian of 180° longitude, roughly down the middle of the Pacific Ocean and halfway around the world from the Greenwich Meridian. The IDL is deviated east or west away from the meridian eight places to prevent any anomalies regarding the date at a particular place.

The difference between the International Date Line (180° longitude) and Indian Standard Time (82°30' East) is 97°30' longitude. International Date Line passes through the Bering Strait (Pacific Ocean).
Latitudes are the angular distance of a point on the earth’s surface, measured in degrees from the center of the earth.
An equator is the 0° circle of latitude (parallel). It is the imaginary line on the spheroid’s surface, equidistant from the poles, dividing it into the northern and southern hemispheres.
On earth, the equator is larger than any other latitude. Hence, it is a
great circle

As the latitudes move away from the equator towards the poles, their length decreases. The length of the earth’s equator is appx. 40090 km (approx. 24911 miles). Out of its total length, 78.7% lies across water bodies and only 21.3% lies across land. The equatorial region receives almost vertical rays of the sun throughout the year, hence the difference between the maximum and minimum range of temperature is next to zero.
Tropic of Cancer, Equator and Tropic of Capricorn, all the three pass through Africa. The Tropic of Capricorn & Equator pass through South America.

chapters.title: The Earth · The Tropic of Cancer

runs: The Tropic of Cancer is
degrees latitude north of the equator. Due to the axial tilt of the earth and its revolution, the Tropic of Cancer (
latitude) starts getting oriented towards the sun by 21st March.
Three months later i.e. by
21st June
the Tropic of Cancer is aligned in a way that it receives the vertical rays of the Sun. Hence
21st June
is known as the day of the summer solstice in Northern Hemisphere.
The Tropic of Cancer passes through the following countries/ regions of the world–
(1) Algeria
(2) Niger
(3) Libya
(4) Egypt
(5) Saudi Arabia
(6) United Arab Emirates
(7) Oman
(8) India
(9) Bangladesh
(10) Myanmar
(11) China
(12) Taiwan
(13) Mexico
(14) The Bahamas
(15) Mauritania
(16) Mali
(17) Western Sahara
22nd December

, when the sun is vertically overhead of The Tropic of Capricorn it is called winter solstice. Since the Earth is inclined at an angle of 23⁰30', when the sun’s rays fall at a perpendicular angle (90°) at the Tropic of Capricorn, then at the same time the Tropic of cancer will witness an inclination of90°–47°= 43°.
The angular difference between the Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn is 23⁰30' + 23⁰30' = 47°.

chapters.title: The Earth · The Tropic of Capricorn

runs: The 23°30' South latitude in the Southern Hemisphere is known as the Tropic of Capricorn. On 21/22 December the sun shines vertically overhead the Tropic of Capricorn, and it is the longest day in the Southern Hemisphere receiving sunlight for the maximum duration.

During this time there is low air pressure in the Southern Hemisphere and thus the region experiences summer. On in contrast the Northern Hemisphere has high air pressure and experiences winter. During this time the sun’s rays fall at an oblique angle on the Tropic of Cancer.
The Tropic of Capricorn passes through the following countries/regions:
(1) Namibia
(2) Australia
(3) Chile
(4) Argentina
(5) Paraguay
(6) Brazil
(7) Tonga
(8) French Polynesia (France)
(9) Botswana
(10) Mozambique
(11) South Africa
(12) Madagascar.
The earth has two kinds of movements – (1) Rotation i.e. rotation of Earth around its own axis. (2) Revolution i.e. the movement of the earth around the sun.

The earth on its axis rotates from west to east. The rotation of the earth causes the phenomena of Day and Night. The earth is tilted on its axis at an angle of 23.5° as a result of which the duration of Day and Night is not always equal.
However, the duration of Day and Night is always equal on the equator as the sun always shines vertically overhead on the equator.
Between
21st March
and
23rd September

the sun shines between the equator and the Tropic of Cancer, as a result of which the Northern Hemisphere receives more than 12 hours of sunlight. Thus the Days are longer and nights are shorter in the Northern Hemisphere during this time.
Similarly, from
23rd September
to
21st March

, the sun shines between the Equator and the Tropic of Capricorn. As a result the Southern Hemisphere receives more than 12 hours of sunlight. As one moves closer to the South Pole the duration of Day keeps on increasing, during this period the South Pole witnesses a 6 month long daytime.

Earth revolves around the sun in an elliptical orbit and completes one revolution around the sun in approx 365 days and 6 hours. Thus because of revolution and axial tilt, the angle of insolation changes throughout the year. Solstices occur twice a year.
Summer solstice

– On 20/21st June the sun shines vertically overhead at Tropic of Cancer. This phenomenon is called the summer solstice. On 20/21st June the Northern Hemisphere experiences the lengthiest day. The phenomenon is also called
June solstice
. During this time the Southern Hemisphere witnesses the shortest day.
Winter solstice
– On
21/22nd December,

the sun shines vertically overhead at the Tropic of Capricorn. This phenomenon is called the winter solstice. During this time the Southern Hemisphere witnesses the lengthiest day and Northern Hemisphere witnesses the shortest day. This phenomenon is also known as the
December solstice
On
20/21st March The Vernal Equinox
occurs and on
22/23rd September The Autumnal Equinox

. During this time the length of day and night is equal. Due to the revolution and axial tilt of the Earth, the Tropic of Cancer (23.5° North Latitude) in the Northern Hemisphere starts getting oriented towards the sun from 21 March and by 21st June the sun is vertically overhead the Tropic of Cancer.
The size of the shadow of any object depends upon the size of the object, the distance from the sun and the angle it creates with respect to the rays of the sun.
The size of the shadow will be the smallest when the angle is least.
When the angle created is 0° there will be no shadow formation.
The shadow formation in the Northern Hemisphere will be at a minimum on 21st June.

chapters.title: The Earth · Origin of the Earth

runs: Earth is one of the planets in the solar system. Its origin is not different from that of the other planets. Different scholars have propounded different theories regarding the subject.
One of the earliest works on the subject was presented by
Immanuel Kant
. He propounded the theory of nebulous material.
In 1755 A.D. Immanuel Kant presented the Gaseous hypothesis. Later in 1796 A.D.,
Laplace
presented his research on the topic which came to be known as
Nebular Hypothesis
Chamberlin
and
Moulton
proposed the
Chamberlin-Moulton planetesimal hypothesis

to describe the formation of the solar system. The theory was based on the idea that a star passed close enough to the sun early in its life to cause tidal bulges to form on its surface, causing the material to be ejected repeatedly from the sun. Due to the gravitational effects of the passing star, materials would cool and condense into numerous small bodies, which they called planets.
In 1919 the famous British scientist
James Jeans
propounded the
Tidal Hypothesis
and another scientist
Sir Harold Jeffreys
made some corrections to it. After some years, the theory of a wandering star around the sun started getting acceptance. The theory was called
Binary Theories

In 1943, Otto Schmidt propounded the interstellar dust hypothesis. He proposed that the sun, in its present form, passed through a dense interstellar cloud and emerged enveloped in a cloud of dust and gas.
Otto Schmidt
of Russia and
Carl Weizsacker
of Germany revised the Nebular Hypothesis.

They believed dust like ‘Solar Nebula’ with heavy helium and hydrogen surrounds the sun. A disk-shaped cloud was created by the friction of particles in the solar Nebula. The planet was formed due to the accretion process.
In modern times the most accepted theory regarding the origin of Universe is the
Big Bang Theory
also known as
expanding Universe Theory
. Universal expansion was proved by
Edwin Hubble

in 1920. According to the Big Bang Theory, a violent explosion of a tiny body occurred which resulted in huge expansion and the change of some particles into an energy form. Due to this expansion, some energy got converted into matter. This happened 13.7/13.8 billion years ago.
Another proof of this Edwin Hubble concluded that galaxies are drifting
apart

. This is important observational evidence consistent with the hypothesis of an expanding Universe. After initial expansion, the universe cooled sufficiently to allow the formation of subatomic particles and later simple atoms. Giant clouds of these elements later combined due to gravity eventually forming early stars and galaxies. The galaxies further broke down resulting in the formation of stars and stars broke down (ran out of fuel) resulting in the formation of early planets.

In 1907 John Joly, used his knowledge of mineralogy to figure out the age of different minerals. According to him certain rock-forming minerals were often characterized by the presence of small circular dark spots or concentric rings. He called it the
Mineral Halo
Professor
H.H. Russell
used Uranium –Lead and Thorium-Lead to determine the age of Earth. According to it the age of our planet is 2 billion and 25 crore years and 4 billion and 60 crore year old respectively.

Radiometric dating has proven to be the most successful way offiguring out the Earth’s age. As Uranium and Thorium are found in one form or the other in different quantities in every rock formation, the Uranium Dating Technique to determine the age of Earth becomes very useful.

Geological History of Earth follows the major events in Earth’s past based on the geological time scale. The first efforts to understand the Geological History of Earth were made by a French naturalist Comte de Buffon. At present the geological time scale is used, which is a system of chronological dating that relates geological states to time.
The primary defined divisions of time are eons. Eons are divided into eras which are in turn divided into periods and epochs.
Pre Cambrian Era

– Earth was initially molten due to extreme volcanism and frequent collisions with other bodies. Water began accumulating in the atmosphere. The only flora present at this time was seagrasses. In the warm oceans emergence of spineless creatures also took place.
A geological period is one of the several subdivisions of geological time. Every period is named after its characteristic events.
Cambrian Period
– The waters of the Cambrian period appear to have been widespread and shallow. The seas saw the emergence of creatures with spinal cord along with spinal cord during this period.
Ordovician Period
– By this time process of mountain formation had started and thus period witnessed heavy volcanic activity. Flora and fauna were only limited to the seas.
Silurian Period

– The period witnessed the emergence of terrestrial flora however leaf formation was yet not present. Diversity in the species of flora was also seen. A very prominent phenomenon of this period was large scale development and expansion of coral reefs.
Devonian Period

- The period was a time of great tectonic activity as a result of which it witnessed large scale mountain formations and volcanic activities. Various varieties of Fish emerged and evolved during this period, hence the period is also known as the ‘Age of Fishes’.
Carboniferous period

– Our Earth is made up of different plates. These plates are not stationary but keep moving because of tectonic activity. Hence, these plates are responsible for shifting of the continents and oceanic floors into various parts of the planet. The Carboniferous was a time of active mountain building, as the supercontinent Pangea came together. The supercontinent was surrounded by a large water body. The sea was named Panthalassa by Wegener. The northern part of Pangea i.e. Laurasia (North America, Europe and Asia) and southern part Gondwana (South America, Africa, Madagascar, Peninsular India, Australia and Antarctica).
Permian Period

– During this period, because of geological turmoil, the birth of high mountain ranges was seen in Europe, Asia and Eastern United States of America (Appalachian). Another factor witnessed was the increase in terrestrial species.
Triassic Period

– The period witnessed the emergence of carnivorous aquatic reptiles that had a resemblance to and characteristics of fishes. The period also witnessed the first evolution of terrestrial mammals. Flies and termites also came into the picture during this period along with the origin of dinosaurs.
Jurassic Period
– This period saw the development of the size and diversity of terrestrial reptiles. Some aerial birds such as Archaeopteryx also emerged during this period. This period was dominated by dinosaurs.
Archaeological evidence of
dinosaurs
in India has been found at
Raiyoli in Mahisagar
district of Gujarat and in Bara Simla Hills near the rivers Narmada in Jabalpur district of Madhya Pradesh.
Cretaceous Period
– Geological developments and transformations were very active during this period. As a result the Rocky Mountains, Andes Mountain ranges of Europe and Isthmus of Panama were formed.
The tertiary period has been categorized into different epochs. They are as follows -
Palaeocene Epoch
Eocene Epoch
– The epoch saw the formation of the Indian Ocean, Atlantic Ocean and the Himalayan orogeny.
Oligocene Epoch
- The epoch witnessed expansion of land mass. Geological activity continued in Europe and America and the formation of Alps started.
Miocene Epoch
– The epoch witnessed a lot of geological activity as a result of which Alps mountain range was formed, there was an uplift in the height of the lesser Himalayas and Greater Himalayas.
Pliocene Epoch
– The North Sea, Black Sea, Arabian Sea and Caspian Sea were formed the formation of the Shiwalik range also took place during this epochs.
Quaternary Period
- has been divided into two Epochs Pleistocene Epoch and Holocene Epochs.
Pleistocene Epoch

- The Pleistocene Epoch is defined as the time period that began nearly 2.0 million years ago and lasted until about 10,000 years ago. The most recent ice age occurred then. Almost all the continents experienced glacier formation. The ice-sheets spread was categorized into four different times. Hence, sub-ice ages have been classified and named according to their area of occurrence. They are as follows –
Nebraskan, Kansan Illinois, Iowa and Wisconsin in North America. Similarly, Albrecht Penck and Eduard Bruckner classified the ice ages of Europe. They are as follows – Gunz, Mindel, Riss, Wurm.
Holocene Epoch – The Holocene Epoch began 10,000 years ago.
The melting of ice sheet led to reemergence and expansion of forests in Europe. Aquatic flora and fauna evolved into their present biological characteristics.
The period between 1300 to 1870 A.D. is known as the Little Ice Age. During this time Europe and North America were much colder as compared to the 20th century.

The Earth's crust is made up of rocks. A rock is a naturally occurring solid aggregate of one or more minerals or mineraloids, and it may also contain glass rock fragments, fossils, or organic matter such as plant material in coal. Petrology is the study of rocks, which is an essential component of geology.
The major groups of rocks are defined as igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic.
Igneous Rocks

– Igneous rock is formed through the cool ing and solidification of magma or lava. They are granular in texture and are not found in the stratified form. They are devoid of any kind of fossils. Igneous rocks often have a correlation with volcanic activities. Igneous rocks are hard for water to penetrate. Igneous rock is found both in crystalline and non-crystalline form. They are also known as primary rocks. Igneous rocks are divided into two main categories-
Plutonic or intrusive rocks
– formed when magma cools and crystallises slowly within the earth’s crust. Ex.-granite, gabbros and pegmatite.
Volcanic or extrusive rocks are
– Basalt, volcanic breccias etc.
Sedimentary rocks

– Sedimentary rocks are formed at the Earth’s surface by the accumulation and cementation of fragments of earlier rocks, minerals and organisms or as chemical precipitates and organic growth in water (sedimentation).

Sediments are formed by the weathering of earlier rocks (igneous, sedimentary and metamorphic) by erosion from a source and are then transported to the place of deposition by water, wind, ice and mass movement of glaciers (agents of denudation). After this through the process of lithification, loose, unconsolidated sediments are turned into solid sedimentary rocks.

Many sedimentary rocks are able to retain their specific characteristics in their depository layer, even after lithification. It is the reason why sand stones have multiple layers of different concentrations.
Sedimentary rocks are formed by the accumulation of sediments. There are three basic types of sedimentary rocks-
(i) Sedimentary rocks formed as a result of mechanical processes- Ex - sandstones, shale, conglomerate etc.
(ii) sedimentary rocks - limestone, coal, etc.
(iii) Chemical sedimentary rocks - halite, potassium and magnesium salt etc.
Metamorphic Rock

s – These rocks are formed by subjecting any rock type – sedimentary rock or igneous rock to different temperature and pressure conditions and chemical processes than those in which the original rock was formed. This process is called metamorphism meaning
“change of form”
. The result is a profound change in physical properties and chemistry of the stone. The temperature and pressure required for this process are always higher than those found at the Earth’s surface.
Metamorphosed form of Igneous Rocks –
(1) Granite – Gneiss
(2) Basalt – Schist
(3) Basalt – Amphibolite
Metamorphosed form of Sedimentary Rocks -
(1) Shale – Slate
(2) Limestone – Marble
(3) Chalk and Dolomite – Marble
(4) Sandstone – Quartzite
(5) Conglomerate - Gneiss
Metamorphosed form of Metamorphic Rocks –
(1) Slate – Phyllite
(2) Phyllite – Schist
(3) Gabbro – Serpentine
A volcano is a rupture in the crust of a planetary mass object, such as Earth, that allows hot lava, volcanic ash and gases to escape from a magma chamber below the surface.
Among the gases emitted through a volcanic eruption the, highest quantity is that of
water vapor
(H₂O). Other gases emitted are
carbon-dioxide
(CO₂),
sulphur dioxide
(SO₂),
hydrogen
(H₂),
carbon-monoxide
(CO),
hydrogen chloride
(HCl),
hydrogen fluoride
(HF) and
helium
(He).
Magma

is made of molten rock and is stored in the Earth’s interior. lava is magma that reaches the Earth's surface with temperature ranging from about 600°C 1200°C. When Lava reaches the surface it cools to form
igneous rocks
. The composition of almost all lava of the earth’s crust is dominated by silica (SiO₂) materials. Based on the silicate, lava can be classified into two types-
Acidic Lava
and
Basic Lava
Acidic lava
is highly dense and sticky in nature and has high silica content. Basic lava, on the other hand is less dense and has low silica content.
Intrusive igneous rocks
are formed when lava cools and solidifies before reaching the earth’s surface. Igneous rocks are of two types – intrusive and extrusive.
Caldera
is an extended version of a volcanic vent.
A
geyser

is a spring characterized by intermittent discharge of water ejected turbulently and accompanied by steam. Generally, all Geyser field sites are located near the active volcanic areas, and the geyser effect is due to the proximity of magma. For example the Old Faithful Geyser of Yellowstone National Park in the United States of America.
A
fumarole
is the last phase in a volcanic activity. It is an opening that emits steam and gases. The name
solfatara
is given to fumarole that emit sulfurous gases.
Mount Katmai
of Alaska (USA) is known as the Valley of Ten Thousand Smokes. Volcanoes are categorized according to their level of activeness–
Active Volcano
– An active volcano has its vent open and keeps emitting smoke, gas and lava often. At present
Mount Kilauea
is the one of the world's most active volcano. Situated on Hawaiian Islands of the USA it has been in an active state from between 1983 to 2018.
The top three most active volcanoes are – Kilauea, Mount Etna and Piton de la Fournaise.
On the basis of size, the
largest active volcano
on Earth is
Mauna Loa
, situated on Hawaiian Islands.
Mount Etna
is an active volcano on the east coast of the island of Sicily in Italy. It stands 3357 meters tall.
Stromboli

is an active volcano on Stromboli Island, north of Sicily in the Tyrrhenian Sea. The volcano has erupted many times and is constantly active with minor eruptions, often visible from many points on the island and from the surrounding sea, giving rise to Island’s nickname
“Lighthouse of the Mediterranean.”
Nevados Ojos del Salado is an active volcano in the Andes on the Argentina Chile border and the highest active volcano in the world at 6879 m.
Mount Erebus
is an active volcano located on Ross
Island in Antarctica.
Barren Island
is an island located in the Andaman Sea, dominated by Barren Volcano, the only confirmed active volcano in South Asia.
Mount Fuji
located on Honshu Island in an active volcano in Japan. Presently Mount Vesuvius (Italy) is an a active volcano.
Mount St. Helens
is a volcano located in Skamania County, Washington, in the Pacific Northwest region of the United States. It is also known as the
'Fujiyama of America'
Dormant Volcanoes

- A dormant volcano is one that has not erupted recently but is expected to do so again. Kilimanjaro volcano of Tanzania. It has three main volcanic cones- Kibo, Mawenzi and Shira. Among these peaks Kibo is dormant while Mawenzi and Shira are extinct. Damavand of Iran.
Extinct Volcano
– Extinct volcanoes are those that scientist consider unlikely to erupt again because the volcano no longer has a magma supply. For example- Kulal (Kenya) in Africa and Koh-e-Sultan of Pakistan.

An earthquake is the shaking of the surface of the Earth, resulting from the sudden release of energy in the earth’s lithosphere that creates seismic waves. An earthquake's point of initial rupture is called its
seismic
focus or
hypocenter

. The epicenter is the point at ground level directly above the hypocenter. The epicenter is the point on the Earth's surface directly above the hypocenter. All natural earthquakes occur in the lithosphere. There are three basic types of seismic waves –
Primary Waves

(P-wave) – They are similar to sound waves. They are also known as longitudinal waves. P-waves travel faster than any other waves. Their intensity of travel depends upon the density of the rock they encounter. Since they are the fastest traveling seismic wave, they are the first signal from an earthquake to arrive at any affected location or at a seismograph.
P–waves
may be transmitted through gases, liquids and solids.
Secondary Waves
(S-waves) – They are similar to light waves. They are also known as
transverse waves
. These waves arrive after the primary waves and travel slower than the P-waves. The S-waves can travel only through solid materials.
Surface Waves (L-waves)

– These waves travel slower than the other two waves and can travel only through the surface of the earth. Surface waves travel around the globe before reaching the epicenter. Surface waves are the most damaging of all the waves. Surface waves are of two types
(i) Love waves (ii) Rayleigh waves. In these two waves Love waves have higher speed.
The magnitude of an earthquake is the indication of the energy released.
The magnitude of the earthquake is measured on the
Richter scale
and intensity on
Mercalli scale

. The Richter scale was invented in the year 1935 by Charles Francis Richter. The Richter scale is a logarithmic scale whose base is 10. Each step represents a ten-fold increase in amplitude on the seismogram, whereas in terms of energy, each whole number increase corresponds to an increase of about 32 times (31.6) the amount of energy released. Every point on the scale (earthquake waves) denotes an energy release, equivalent to 6 ounces of TNT (Trinitrotoluene).
Seismometer
is used to measure earthquake waves. The term tsunami is borrowed from the Japanese meaning harbor wave.
Tsu means
Harbor
and
nami
means
waves
. Tsunami is caused by earthquakes, volcanic eruptions and other underwater explosions and their destructive power can be enormous affecting entire ocean basins.
The
Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear disaster

was an nuclear accident at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant initiated primarily by a tsunami following an earthquake on 11 March 2011. It led to a nuclear meltdown and the release of radioactivity in the area.
The
Ring of Fire

is a major area in the basin of the Pacific Ocean where many earthquakes and volcanic eruptions occur. The Ring of Fire is sometimes called Circum Pacific belt. About 90% of the world’s earthquakes occur along the Ring of Fire.
There are four main conditions for the occurrence of earthquakes in this region – (1)
Point of interaction between sea and land
Young fold mountainous region
Volcanic Activity
Plate tectonics
– movement and collision of plates.
The region consists of Chile, California, Alaska, Japan, Philippines, New Zealand etc.
The Northwestern part of the India subcontinent is an earthquake prone area. This is because it is the convergence zone of Indian and Eurasian tectonic plates.

The earthquake-prone regions of India are included in the Mid-Continental Belt. The Belt starts from Cape Verde and includes Atlantic Ocean, Mediterranean Sea, and young fold mountain ranges like the Alps, Caucasus and Himalayas. The Mid-Atlantic Belt is a mid ocean belt.

and

separate Asia from Africa. In the east, the
Bering

Europe

is a continent located entirely in the northern hemisphere and mostly in the eastern hemisphere. It is covered by water on three sides. It is bordered by the Arctic Ocean in the north, the Atlantic Ocean to the west and the Mediterranean Sea to the south. There are 49 countries in Europe. [
Note -
5 countries such as Georgia, Azerbaijan, Kazakhstan, Russia and Turkiye are in both continents Asia and Europe].
Africa

is the second largest continent after Asia. The three important latitudes (Tropic of Cancer, Tropic of Capricorn and Equator) pass through Africa. There are 54 countries in the continent of Africa more than any other continent in the world.
The
Strait of Gibraltar
Mediterranean Sea
Suez Canal
Red Sea
and
Arabian Sea
separate Africa from Eurasia. To the east of Africa is the Indian Ocean and to the west is the Atlantic Ocean.
North America

is a continent entirely within the Northern Hemisphere and all within the Western Hemisphere. The continent has been named after the Italian explorer Amerigo Vespucci. There are 23 countries in this continent. It is bordered to the north by the Arctic Ocean, to the east by the Atlantic Ocean and to the west by the Pacific Ocean. South America, Middle America, Mexico and the West Indies are collectively known as Latin America.
South America
is bordered on the west by the Pacific Ocean and on the north and east by the Atlantic Ocean. The
Panama Canal
separates North America from South America. There are 12 countries in South America with Brazil being the largest one.
Antarctica is Earth’s southernmost continent. It contains the geographic South Pole and is situated, almost entirely south of the Antarctic Circle.
Antarctica
, on average, is the coldest, driest and windiest, and has the highest average elevation of all the continents.
The average elevation of the continents is as follows – Antarctica – 2300 m, North America - 760 m, Africa- 585 m, South America – 554 m, Asia – 923 m, Europe
– 302 m, Australia – 330 m. Both Europe and South America have large proportions of their land as plain areas. Percentage wise Europe has more area under plains.
A mountain range is a series of mountains arranged in a linear manner and connected by high ground.
Mountains have a steep slope and pointed summits. Though plateaus are also elevated structures. The main difference between a plateau and a mountain is that
the mountain is an elevated, pointed structure whereas a plateau is an elevated area with a flat top

Most geologists classify a mountain as a landform that rises at least 1000 metres or more above its surrounding areas, landforms having elevation less than 1000 metres are generally classified as hills. Thus those areas having an elevation of 1000 m above sea level and also a high relative height in that area are considered to be mountainous regions. Mountains occupy approx. 25% of the Earth's land area however supports only 12% of the global population.
British Columbia
is called a
Sea of Mountains
, a name given by Molyneux St. John, in his book “The Sea of Mountains: An account of Lord Dufferin’s Tour Through British Columbia in 1876."
Fold mountains
– are mountains that are formed mainly by the effect of folding of layers within the upper part of the Earth’s crust.
The
Andes

is the most important mountain range in South America and also the largest mountain range in the world. It has a length of 7000 km. to 8900 km according to different standard sources. The highest peak of Andes is Aconcagua (6962 m).
The Rocky Mountain
range is the most important mountain range of North America with an approximate length of 4800 km. The highest peak of the Rockies is Mount Elbert (4401 m).
The Himalayas
of South Asia are located at the northern most point of India. Their approximate length is 2500 km. The highest mountain peak in the world i.e.,
Mount Everest
also known as Sagarmatha or Chomolungma (8848.86 m), along with the other highest peaks, is situated in the Himalaya Mountain Range.
The
Southern Alps
are situated in the western part of the South Island of New Zealand. Their tallest peak is
Aoraki/ Mount Cook
The
Alps
are the highest and most extensive mountain range system that is entirely in Europe.
Its highest peak is
Mont Blanc
(4807 mt). The Alps are the most prominent example of young fold Mountains.
The Atlas mountain Range
of Africa stretches around 2500 km through Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia.
Block mountains –
Block mountains are formed as a result of
faulting

caused by tensile and compressive forces. They are also known as fault block mountains or horst mountains. Block mountains represent the upstanding part of the ground between two faults or on either side of a rift valley.
The
Sierra Nevada mountain
of California (USA) is the world’s most extensive block mountains range.
The Black Forest
of Germany and Vosges of France are some more examples of block mountains.
Salt Range
of Pakistan is also an example of block mountains.
Dome Mountain

- The interior of the earth is hot enough to melt rocks. Melted rock sequences together into vast pools of magma beneath the ground. Since it’s less dense than the surrounding rock, it makes its way upward to the surface. If the magma reaches the surface you get a volcano, but if the magma pushes up but doesn’t actually crack through the surface, you get a dome mountain.
The
Cincinnati Arch of USA
Black Hills
, Bighorns are some examples of dome mountains.
Fujiyama
of Japan and
Cotopaxi
of Ecuador are also examples of domed mountains.
Mixed Mountains

– When a lot of complexity is found in the formation of any mountain range then the mountain is called a mix mountain or a complex mountain. For example, Sierra Nevada and Anaconda Mountains Range of the USA.
Residual Mountains
– Residual Mountains are formed as a result of erosion of an existing elevated area. They are also called mountains of denudation. For example -
Pennines
(Europe),
Appalachian
(North America),
Aravallis
(India) etc.
White Mountains
are situated in New Hampshire and Maine (USA)..
Black Mountains
is situated in the State of North Carolina, USA. It is a part of the Great Appalachian Range.
The Black Forest

is a large forested mountain range in southwest Germany. Its highest peak is Feldberg (1493 m). The Rhine is a European river that emerges in the Swiss Alps, then flows mainly through Germany, France and the Netherlands and eventually empties into the North Sea. The cities of
Cologne
and
Bonn
are situated on the banks of the river Rhine. The Black Forest mountains are located on the eastern side of this river and Vosges mountains is located on western side.
Burmese
Arakan Yoma

Mountain Range, located in the western Myanmar, creates a boundary between India and Myanmar. They include the Naga Hills, the Chin Hills, and the Patkai Range which includes the Lushai Hills. The highest peak of Arakan Yoma is
Natma Taung (Mount Victoria)
. The
Khasi Hills
are a part of the Garo-Khasi Jaintia range in the Indian state of Meghalaya.
Mount Titlis
is located in Switzerland. The mountain is made of volcanic lava. The Apennines are located in Italy.
It extends the entire length of Peninsular Italy.
The length of this range is appx. 1350 km.
The tallest peak of this range is
Corno Grande
The
Dinaric Alps
are a mountain range in Europe. They stretch from Italy through Slovenia, Croatia, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Serbia, Montenegro and Kosovo to Albania.
The Jura Mountains extend in the countries, France and Switzerland.
The
Pyrenees

are a range of mountains in southwest Europe that forms a natural border between Spain and France. It also separates the Iberian Peninsula from the rest of continental Europe and extends for about 491 km from the Bay of Biscay to the Mediterranean Sea.
The Great Dividing Range
or the Eastern Highlands is Australia’s most substantial mountain range and the third longest land- based range in the world. Its highest point is
Mount Kosciuszko
located in New South Wales Australia. The elevation of Mount Kosciuszko is 2,228 m.
Denali is also known as
Mount McKinely
is the highest mountain peak in North America with a summit elevation of 6,190 m above sea level. On August 2015, it was decided to change the name of Denali.
Mount Elbrus
is an extinct volcano in the Caucasus Mountains and is considered the highest (5642 m) mountain in Europe and Russia.
Mount Kilimanjaro
is a dormant volcano in Tanzania. It is the highest mountain in Africa (5895 m above sea level).
The
Allegheny Mountain
Range is a part of the Appalachian Mountain Range of North America.
The
Cantabrian Mountain Range
is a system of a mountain range in Spain.
Mount Mackenzie
is located in Canada.
The Golan Heights

is located in the Middle East. It is a basaltic plateau located in the southwest of Syria. Since the 1967 six-day war, the western 2/3rd of the Golan heights has been occupied and administered by Israel and by 1981 it was totally annexed by Israel.
