A plateau, also called a high plain or a tableland, is an area of land with relatively flat terrain that rises significantly above the surrounding region and often has one or more steep sides.
Plateaus can be formed by a number of processes
Glacial Plateau-
Plateaus formed by the erosional and depositional processes of glaciers on mountain ranges, making their tops flat and sitting between other mountain ranges.
Fluvial Plateau-

These plateaus have been formed by continuous deposits of fluvial sediments brought by the rivers. The Panna Plateau, Bhander Plateau, Rewa Plateau and Rohtas Plateau are some examples of Fluvial Plateaus.
Intermontane Plateau-

These are high plateaus enclosed by mountain ranges and are among the most widely distributed and topographically diverse plateau types. Intermontane plateaus are landforms that are surrounded by mountain rims, these plateaus are enclosed by high mountain chains; they are the highest plateaus in the world.
The
Tibetan Plateau
is also known as
Qinghai-Tibetan

covers an area of approximately 2.5 million sq. km and has an average elevation of4500 m. Chang Tang is located in the western and northern Tibet extending into the southern edges of Xinjiang as well as southeastern Ladakh (India). It is the highest plateau in the world and a good example of an intermontane plateau.
The
Pamir Knot
is known as the Roofofthe World.
Note: - The term roof of the world is first used for Pamir Knot, however it is now also used to refer to the Tibetan Plateau.
The southern border of Central Asia is determined by the Pamir Knot.
The Pamir Plateau in Central Asia is at the junction of the
Himalayas
with
Tien Shan
Karakoram
Kunlun
Hindu Kush
and
Suleman ranges
. They are among the world’s highest mountains. The Bolivia, Peru and Colombia Plateaus of South America and the Mexican Platea of Mexico are also some examples of Intermontane Plateaus.
Piedmont Plateau-
The name Piedmont comes from the French term for the same physical region, literally meaning ‘foothill’, ultimately from Latin “Pedemontium” meaning at the foothills of mountains.

The Piedmont Plateau region located in the Eastern United States and the Patagonia Plateaus of South America are great examples of Piedmont Plateaus. The Patagonia Plateau of South America is very rich in mineral resources.
Domed Plateaus-
These are formed when a landmass is uplifted by folding into a broad dome. The Plateau of Ozark (USA) is a good example of a domed Plateau.
Continental Plateau-

A Continental Plateau is a broad protuberance of the surface of the lithosphere coinciding approximately with a continent but including also the continental shelf. The Indian Peninsula, the Arabian Plateau, Plateau of Australia and the South African Plateau etc. are examples of Continental Plateaus.
The
Iberian Peninsula

also known as Iberia is located in the southwest corner of Europe. The peninsula is principally divided between Spain and Portugal, comprising most of their territory. It is the second largest European peninsula, after the
Scandinavian Peninsula.
The
Meseta plateau
of the Iberian Peninsula is located in Spain and has an average elevation of 610-760 m. The capital of Spain Madrid is located at its center.
Coastal Plateau-
A plateau located near sea coasts is classified as a Coastal Plateau. India’s Coromandel Coast is an example of a Coastal plain.
Volcanic Plateau-
A volcanic plateau is a plateau produced by volcanic activity. Chiefly there are two types:
(a) Lava Plateaus-
formed by highly fluid basaltic lava during numerous successive eruptions through numerous vents without violent explosions.
(b) Pyroclastic Plateau-

Plateaus are produced by massive pyroclastic flow and they are underlain by pyroclastic rocks: agglomerates, tephra, volcanic ashes cemented into tuffs, the magic offelsics composition. Pyroclastic Plateaus are also called ignimbrite plateaus.

Plateaus of New Zealand, South Africa, North and South Argentina, Brazil, Western USA, Mexico, France and Siberia are some examples of a Volcanic Plateaus. The Plateau of Peninsular India is also an example of a Volcanic Plateau.
A valley is a low area between hills or mountains typically with a river flowing through it. In geology a valley is a long depression with very little width.
A
rift valley

is a lowland region formed by the interaction of Earth tectonic plates. It is a linear-shaped lowland between several highlands and mountain ranges created by the action of a geological rift or fault.
A rift valley is formed on a divergent plate boundary, a crustal extension or spreading apart of the surface, which is subsequently further dependent on the forces of erosion.
The Death Valley
situated mainly in California (USA) is an example of a rift valley.
Devils Golf Course
is a large salt pan on the floor of Death Valley, located in the northern Mojave Desert within
Death Valley National Park
. The park is located mainly in eastern California.
In the Holocene era this area was covered with water reaching a depth of 30 ft. When the water of the region dried up it left behind the dissolved salt in it.

Death Valley is the point of the lowest elevation in North America (-86 m) and the second lowest point in the Western Hemisphere only after Laguna del Carbon of Argentina (-105 m). During summers the temperature in Death Valley can rise up to 56.7°C. It is the hottest and driest place in the USA. Recently it was declared the hottest place on the planet (from the point of view of air temperature).

The Panjshir Valley (literally the valley of five lions) is a valley in northeastern Afghanistan, north of Kabul, near the Hindu Kush Mountain Range. It is divided by the Panjshir River. The valley was a major battleground during the Soviet war.
The
Taylor Valley
of Antarctica was discovered by Robert Falcon Scott in the year 1903. He designated this valley as the Valley of the Dead.
Bhutan and Tibet
Silicon Valley

is a region in the southern part of the San Francisco Bay Area in Northern California. The place is known as a center of high-tech industries, with major emphasis now partly shifted from manufacturing to research, development, marketing and software.
The Great Artesian Basin

located in Australia, is the largest and deepest artesian basin in the world. The basin provides the only reliable resource of fresh water to much of inland Australia. Spreading across about 1.7 million sq.km, it is located between the Great Dividing Range and the medial uplands.
The Great Basin
is the largest area of the contiguous endorheic watershed in North America located in the arid region between the Rocky Mountain Range and the Sierra Nevada.
Major Grasslands/natural vegetation of the world
The Columbia Plateau
lies to the north of the Great Basin and the Mojave and Sonoran deserts lie to the south of it.

Desert is a barren area of landscape where little precipitation occurs and consequently, living conditions are hostile for plants and animals. About 1/3rd of the land surface of the world is arid or semiarid. Regions receiving precipitation of less than 25 cm annually are categorized as deserts. Deserts can be classified by the amount of precipitation, by the temperature that prevails, by the causes of their dryness or by their geographical location.
Tropical hot deserts

are generally found on the continental interiors and often western side between 15° to 30° north or south of the equator. Most of the major deserts of the world lie in areas crossed by the trade winds.

According to German scientist Dr. Gerhard Knies, the amount of energy that is received from the sun by the word's desearts in 6 hours is more than the amount of energy consumed by the entire humankind in a year. Hence deserts are a very prominent source of renewable energy.
The Sahara Desert

is the largest non-polar desert in the world. The desert comprises much of North Africa, excluding the fertile regions on the Mediterranean Sea coast. It occupies a total area of 3600000 sq. miles. The Sahara covers large parts of Algeria, Chad, Egypt, Libya, Mali, Mauritania, Morocco, Niger, Western Sahara, Sudan and Tunisia. The main phenomena behind the formation of African and Euro Asian deserts are –
1. Their proximity to cold ocean currents which run along the west coast. These cold ocean currents cool the air and make it harder for the air to hold moisture.
2. Most of these deserts are located far away from the moisture-laden trade winds.
The Atacama
is a desert plateau in South America on the Pacific Coast, west of Andes Mountains. It is the driest desert in the world.

The Atacama Desert is rich in metallic mineral resources such as copper, gold, silver and iron, as well as non-metallic minerals including important deposits ofboron, lithium, sodium nitrate and potassium salts. It is the world’s largest supplier of sodium nitrate. The Atacama Desert occupies the narrow coast of northern Chile and southern Peru.
The Kalahari Desert

is located in the Southern Hemisphere. The Kalahari Desert is a large semi-arid sandy savanna in Southern Africa, extending for 9,30,000 square kilometers covering much of Botswana, parts of Namibia and regions of South Africa.
The Dasht-e-Lut

is a large salt desert located in the provinces of Kerman and Sistan and Baluchistan, Iran. According to NASA, it is the world’s hottest desert. The Aqua satellite of NASA, in the year 2005 measured the surface temperature of this desert and found it to be as high as 70.7°C, making it the hottest desert (based on surface temperature) in the world.
The Thar Desert,

also known as the Great Indian Desert is a large arid region in the northwestern part of the Indian subcontinent and forms a natural boundary between India and Pakistan. It is the largest desert in South Asia. The Thar Desert is the most densely populated desert in the world, with a population density of 83 people per/km².
The Taklamakan Desert

is a desert in southwestern Xinjiang Province in north west China. It is bounded by the Kunlun mountains to the south, the Pamir mountains to the west Tian Shan to the north, and the Gobi Desert in the east.
The Sonoran Desert

occurs primarily in Mexico. More than two thirds of its total area is in Baja California, Baja California Sur, and the state of Sonora. It covers large parts of the southwestern United States in Arizona and California. The western portion of the United States – Mexico border passes through the Sonoran Desert.
The Karakum Desert

, is a desert in Central Asia. Its name means "black sand" in Turkic languages, in reference to the dark soil that lies beneath the sandy surface of much of the desert. It occupies much of the area of Turkmenistan and a smaller part of Kazakhstan.
The Karakum Desert
is home to the Darvaza gas Crater. The area has significant oil and natural gas deposits.
The Gibson Desert

is a large desert that covers a large dry area in the State of Western Australia. It is the 5th largest desert in Australia, after the Great Victoria Deseart, Great Sandy Deseart, Tanami Deseart and Simpson Desert.
Al Nafud

is a desert in Northern Saudi Arabia. The discovery of approximately 88000-90000 years old fossilized human finger bone in Al Nafud in 2016 by Dr. Mathieu Duval of Griffith University provided the earliest evidence of modern humans outside Africa and the Levant.
The Rub’al Khali Desert
is located in Saudi Arabia, Oman, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen are the largest contiguous sand desert in the world.Famous oil fields, Shaybah and Ghawar are located in this desert.
The Kyzylkum Desert
is divided between Kazakhstan, Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. The desert is well known for its deposits of gold, uranium, copper, aluminium and silver, natural gas and oil.
Dasht-e-Kavir
is a large desert located in Iran.
The Gobi Desert

is a cold desert found in a temperate region. It covers parts of northern China and of southern Mongolia. The Gobi Desert is notable in history as part of the great Mongol Empire and as the location of several important cities along the Silk Road.
Patagonia Desert
is a cold desert and also the largest desert in Argentina. It is located primarily in Argentina with small parts in Chile and is bounded by the Andes, to its west and the Atlantic Ocean to its east.

A grassland is an area of land that mostly contains grasses. There are wild grasses and there may be some trees. From the hot equatorial region to the cold polar region, grasslands are found all over the world. However, their characteristics and physical attributes change with the change in the climate. Thus, based on the climatic factors the grassland can be categorized into two parts
1. Tropical Grasslands-
These are located near the equator (10° to 25° North or South Latitudes), between the Tropic of Cancer and Tropic of Capricorn. The Tropical Grasslands are also known as Savannas. The
Savanna

grasslands are mostly found in East Africa. They are also found in the Orinoco basin (Venezuela and Colombia), Brazil, Honduras and the southern parts of India. These grasslands are known by different names in different parts of the world. In Africa, they are known as Savanna,
Llanos
in Venezuela and Colombia. Campos in Brazil, Paraguay, Argentina and Uruguay.
Selvas
(Selva) are tropical evergreen rainforests in the Amazon Basin.
2. Temperate Grasslands-

Located between 30° to 60° North and South Latitudes. Due to greater territorial expansion in the Northern Hemisphere, these grasslands (in Northern Hemisphere) may extend up 60° North Latitude. The major temperate grasslands include the
Velds
of Africa, the
Pampas
of Argentina, the
Steppes
of Eurasia, the
Prairies
of North America, and the Downs of Australia.
The Prairie grasslands are found in North America.
The Pampas grasslands are mostly found in Argentina, though they also extend to Uruguay and Brazil.
The temperate grasslands found in Eurasia (Eastern Europe and Central Asia) are known as steppes. The temperate grasslands found in South Africa are called velds.
Downs are temperate grasslands found in Australia.

a landlocked country located in south Asia. Afghanistan is bordered by Pakistan in the east and south including Pakistan- administered Kashmir claimed by India, Iran in the west, Turkmenistan, Uzbekistan and Tajikistan in the north and China in the northeast.
Myanmar

also known as Burma is a country in Southeast Asia. Myanmar is bordered by India and Bangladesh to its northwest and west respectively, Laos and Thailand to its east and southeast respectively and China to its north and northeast.
China

has the longest combined land border in the world. China borders 13 nations, more than any other country except Russia which borders 14 countries. The
Horn of Africa
also known as Somali Peninsula is a peninsula in East Africa. The Horn of Africa denotes the region containing the countries of Djibouti, Eritrea, Ethiopia and Somalia.
Zambia

is a landlocked country in South Central Africa. It neighbours the Democratic Republic of the Congo to the North, Tanzania to the northeast, Malawi to the east and Mozambique to the southeast, Zimbabwe and Botswana to the south, Namibia to the Southwest and Angola to the west.
Sierra Leone
is a country on the southwest coast of West Africa.
Israel
is a country located in Western Asia in the Middle East. It has land borders with Lebanon to the north, Syria to the northeast, Jordan on the east, and Egypt to the southwest.

The Scandinavian Peninsula is a peninsula of Eurasia located in Northern Europe which roughly comprises the mainland of Sweden, the mainland of Norway. However on the basis of Geography Scandinavia comprises of Sweden, Norway and Denmark.
Culturally and historically,
Scandinavian countries
comprise Sweden, Norway, Finland, Denmark and Iceland.
The Balkans also known as the
Balkan Peninsula

is a geographical area in southeastern Europe. The Balkan Peninsula is bordered by the Adriatic Sea on the northwest, the Ionian Sea on the southwest, the Aegean Sea in the south and the Black Sea in the northeast. The region takes its name from the Balkan Mountains that stretch throughout the whole of Bulgaria from the Serbian-Bulgarian borders to the Black Sea.
The Balkan states consist mainly of countries- Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Bulgaria, Croatia, Greece, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Romania and Serbia, Slovenia and the European Turkiye.

and North
Macedonia
are
landlocked countries
Lithuania

is situated along the eastern shore of the Baltic Sea. Its capital and largest city is Vilnius. Lithuania shares land borders with Belarus (678.8 km), Latvia (588.1 km), Poland (104.3 km) and Russia (253.7 km).
Great Britain comprises England, Wales and Scotland.
The total area of the United Kingdom (Great Britain + Northern Ireland) is 243,610 sq. km out of which 53% of the area is under England.
Oceania
is a geographical region comprising of 14 countries, which are divided into 4 sub group Australia & New Zealand, Melanesia, Micronesia and Polynesia. Australia is the largest country in this region.
Canada

has the longest coastline in the world (202,080 km), followed by Norway (83281 km.) Indonesia (54716 km), Greenland (44087 km), Russia (37,653 km) and Philippines (36,289 km). It is bounded by Kazakhstan to the northeast, Russia to the northwest, Azerbaijan to the southwest, Iran to the south and Turkmenistan to the southeast.
Central America
consists of 7 countries, Belize, Costa Rica, El Salvador, Guatemala, Honduras, Nicaragua and Panama.
A dependent territory is a territory that does not possess full political independence or sovereignty as a sovereign state yet remains politically outside the controlling state's integral area.
Dependent Territories under France:
Martinique, French Polynesia, French Guiana, Reunion, New Caledonia, etc.
Dependent Territories Under Denmark:

Greenland is an autonomous region of the Kingdom of Denmark. However, from a geographical point of view, Greenland is a part of the North American continent. Three-quarters of Greenland (about 80%) is covered by permanent ice sheets.
The Faroe Islands are a North Atlantic archipelago, located north of the United Kingdom and about halfway between Norway and Iceland. It is an autonomous region of the Kingdom of Denmark.
Dependent Territories under the United States of America:-
American Samoa

is an unincorporated territory of the United States located in the South Pacific Ocean east of Australia. Since 1900 CE the islands have been an unincorporated territory of the United States of America.
Puerto Rico
is an unincorporated territory of the USA located in the northeast Caribbean Sea, southeast of Miami, Florida. Puerto Rico was discovered by Christopher Columbus in 1493 CE.
The U.S. Virgin Islands
in the Caribbean is an unincorporated and organized territory of the United States. It is located east of Puerto Rico.
Midway Atoll
is an unorganized, unincorporated territory of the United States. It is located in the North Pacific Ocean.
Dependent Territories under Portugal:
The Azores
are an autonomous region of Portugal. It is an archipelago composed of nine volcanic islands in the North Atlantic Ocean.
Madeira
is an autonomous region of Portugal. It is a volcanic archipelago situated in the North Atlantic Ocean.
Dependent Territories of Spain:
The Canary Islands
are a Spanish archipelago and the southernmost autonomous community of Spain located in the Atlantic Ocean.
Ceuta
is a Spanish autonomous region on the North Coast of Africa, separated from Cadiz province on the Spanish mainland by the Strait of Gibraltar.
Melilla
is a Spanish autonomous city located on the north coast of Africa, sharing a border with Morocco.
The Balearic Islands
are an archipelago of Spain in the western Mediterranean Sea, near the eastern coast of the Iberian Peninsula.
Dependent Territories under Norway:
Bouvet Island

is an island in the southern part of the Atlantic Ocean. It belongs to Norway and is not subject to the Antarctic Treaty (which says that land south of 60° S, including Antarctica, does not belong to any country). Apart from it

The Hydrosphere is the total volume of water on the surface of our planet. Although the Earth’s Hydrosphere has been around for longer than 4 billion years, it continues to change and rise. This is caused by seafloor spreading and continental drift. Hydrosphere occupies more than 2/3 of the total surface of the Earth.
Hydrosphere covers about 71% (70.9%) of Earth’s surface. There is only one world ocean but the continents divide the ocean into five largest distinct parts -
The Pacific Ocean is the largest in the world.
Oceanic Relief is a part of lithospheric Relief.

Hypsographic curve describes the distribution of Earth's surface elevations and ocean depth relative to sea level. We read the hypsographic curve like a graph with an x-axis (horizontal) and a y-axis (vertical). The x-axis tells us the elevation of the province. The curved line on the graph tells us about the provinces - where we see a change in the slope of the line, we are looking at a different province.
The oceanic crust differs strikingly from the continental crust with respect to rock types, structure, landforms, age and origin. Four major divisions in the ocean relief are
Continental Shelf
- It is the submerged margin of continental mass extending from the shore to the first prominent slope.
Continental Slope
- The slope that extends from the continental shelf down to the ocean deep.
Continental Rise
- This is the gently sloping seafloor lying at the foot of the continental slope leading gradually into the Abyssal Plain.
Abyssal Plain

- This is the large expanse of very smooth ocean floor found at depths of 3000 to 6000 meters In fact they are the most widespread landforms on the Earth and occupy almost 76% of the total oceanic area.
Oceanic trenches

are narrow, deep depressions in the seafloor representing the line of subduction of an oceanic lithosphere plate. The ocean trenches are the lowest areas on Earth’s surface and occupy almost 7% of the ocean’s relief. They have very steep slopes. Examples of oceanic trenches include the Mariana Trench (Challenger Deep in the Marina Trench), Tonga Trench and Kuril-Kamchatka Trench etc. Other important oceanic reliefs are -
Oceanic Ridge
- formed by lava, that erupts beneath the sea and cools to form solid rocks.
(ii)
Mid Ocean Ridge
- an underwater mountain system formed by plate tectonics.
(iii)
Guyot

- A Guyot, also known as a tablemount is an isolated underwater volcanic mountain with a flat top below the surface of the sea. They are commonly found in the Pacific Ocean, but they have been identified in all the oceans except the Arctic Ocean.
(iv)
Submarine Canyon
- Narrow steep-sided valleys that cut into continental slopes and continental rises of the ocean.
Fracture Zone
- A linear oceanic feature often hundreds, even thousands of kilometers long. They are a consequence of plate tectonics.
Similarly, other ocean relief features include island arcs, atolls, coral reefs, submerged volcanoes, sea-scarps etc.
Mid Atlantic Ridge

is a mid-ocean ridge, a divergent tectonic plate or constructive plate boundary located on the floor of the Atlantic Ocean and part of the most extensive mountain range in the world. In the North Atlantic it separates the Eurasian and North American plates and in South Atlantic it separates the African & South American plates.
The
Ninety East
Ridge is a ridge on the Indian Ocean floor named for its near by parallel strike along the 90th meridian at the center of the Eastern Hemisphere.

An ocean current is a continuous directed movement of sea -water. Surface ocean currents are mainly driven by the prevailing winds and by the rotation of the Earth. Deep-ocean currents, which flow thousands of meters below the ocean surface are driven by differences in water density caused by variation in temperature and salinity. In general, the main cause of ocean currents are wind, differences in water density and tides.
The main causes of ocean currents are–
(i) Differential heating of the equatorial and polar oceans.
(ii) Trade and anti-trade winds
(iii) Coriolis effect
(iv) Variation in salinity and temperature of the oceans.
(v) Configuration of the coastline and ocean floor.
(vi) Gravity
The oceanic currents play a huge role in regulating the planet’s temperature.
Based on the temperature, the ocean currents can be categorized into two types -
warm ocean currents
and
cold ocean currents
Factors Responsible for Change in Direction of Ocean Currents Incluid:
Configuration of the coast
- When a landmass lies perpendicular to the prevailing current, the obstruction thus caused deviates the current to move parallel to the landmass.
(ii)
Ocean floor reliefs
- The diversified ocean floor with distinctive reliefs can also affect the oceanic currents and their direction.
(iii)
Seasonal Variations
- for example, the monsoonal winds change the direction of the ocean currents.
(iv)
The Earth’s Rotation

- The Earth’s rotation deflects freely moving objects including ocean currents, to the right. In the northern hemisphere, this is a clockwise direction (e.g. the circulation of the Gulf Stream Drift and the Canary Current). In the southern hemisphere it is an anti-clockwise direction (e.g. the Brazilian Current and the West Wind Drift).
Currents of Atlantic Ocean
Under the influence of trade winds the North Equatorial Warm Current flows east to west from African coast in the east to the West Indies.
Antilles Current

- Northeastern coast of South America the North Equatorial Current splits into two branches. One branch flows northward, east of the Antilles (West Indies) as Antilles Current and it joins the Florida Current past the outer Bahamas. The other branch passes into the Caribbean Sea as the Caribbean Current and flows west through the Caribbean Sea, then north through the Yucatan Channel into the Gulf of Maxico.
Florida Current
- Under the influence of the trade winds the current flows from the GulfofMexico towards the Straits of Florida. Here it adjoins the Antilles Current.
Gulf Stream

- When the Florida current and Antilles current join together, they are collectively known as the Gulf Stream. The Gulf Stream is a warm and swift Atlantic Ocean current that follows the eastern coastline of the United States.
Canary Cold Current
- It flows southwestward along the northwest coast of Africa as far south as Senegal before turning westward to join the Atlantic North Equatorial Current.
East Greenland Current
- The current travels along the eastern coast of Greenland in southward and southwestward.
Labrador Cold Current
- The current flows from Baffin
Ocean Currents
Bay and the Davis Strait and travels along the coast of Labrador in southward.
North Atlantic Drift/Current

- The current originates between 45º North Latitude and 45º West Longitude. This current is responsible for carrying the Gulf Stream to Europe. Countries like Norway which are located in a sub-polar region benefit the most from this drift of current. This is because during winters northern Europe receives heavy snowfall, thus the warm North Atlantic Drift/Current prevents extreme cold in the region and also keeps the harbors ice-free. As a result, the North Atlantic Warm Drift/Current is also known as the ‘Blanket of Europe’.
Brazil Current
is a warm current. At 40º South Latitude, the
Falkland Current
meets the Brazil Current. Collectively they flow eastward as South Atlantic Drift. Upon reaching the west coast of Africa the current is diverted northwards as the cold
Benguela Current.

It brings the cold polar waters of the west drift into tropical latitudes. Driven by the regular southeast trade winds, the Benguela Current moves equatorward in a northwesterly direction to join the South Equatorial Current. This completes the circulation of the currents in the South Atlantic.
2.Currents of Indian Ocean

- As in the other oceans, the currents of the South Indian Ocean form a circuit. The South Equatorial Current turns Southward and divides into the Madagascar Current and Mozambique Current. These currents merge as Agulhain Current with the West Wind Drift, flowing eastwards and turning equatorward as the West Australian Current (cool current). In the northern Indian Ocean, there is a complete reversal of the direction of currents between summer and winter, due to the changes in monsoon winds. In summer from June to October, when the dominant wind is the southwest Monsoon, the currents are blown from a south - westerly direction as the
southwest Monsoon Drift
. This is reversed in winter, beginning in December, when the northeast Monsoon blows the currents from the north-east as the north-east Monsoon Drift.
Currents of Pacific Ocean
- The pattern of circulation in the Pacific is similar to that of the Atlantic except for modifications that can be expected from the greater size and more open nature of the Pacific.

- Passing through the Bering Strait and transporting cold water from the Arctic Sea into the Pacific Ocean and the
Sea of Okhotsk
. Again passing through the east coast of Sakhalin Island it is joined by the Okhotsk current to meet the warm Japan Current as of the
Oyashio
East Australian Warm Current

Salinity is the amount of salt dissolved in a body of water. On average, seawater in the world’s oceans has a salinity of approximately 35‰ or 35 parts per thousand. This means that for every 1 kg (1000 grams) of seawater there are 35g of salt dissolved in it.

Lands are the main source of salinity in the oceans and rivers are the main carriers. Other factors responsible for ocean salinity are - evaporation, wind, river water, precipitation, ocean currents and volcanoes etc.

The salinity of the ocean can be divided into horizontal and vertical parameters. The uncertainty regarding the amount of salinity in the vertical dimension has obstructed the devlopment of a principle for measuring vertical salinity. This is because in some places, salinity increases with depth and vice-versa.

The density of ocean water is directly proportional to its salinity. This means that if the density of water increases it is an indicator of an increase in salinity hence with the increase in water density, salinity also increases.

The horizontal distribution of salinity in ocean water is expressed as the degree of saltiness of the water, either as a percentage or more often in parts per thousand Variations are shown in salinity distribution maps by isohalines (lines joining places having an equal degree of salinity). Latitudes have a huge impact on the salinity of the oceans. Salinity is lower than the average
in equatorial waters because of the
heavy daily rainfall
and
high evaporation

. Deserts mainly 25º–30º N and S, waters have high salinity because of the high rate of evaporation caused by high temperatures and low humidity. Waters of the polar region have a salinity of less than 35‰ due to the colder climate with little evaporation and because much fresh water is added from the melting of icebergs as well as by several large poleward-bound rivers, e.g. Ob, Lena, Yenisei etc.
Maximum salinity is found between 20º-40º North Latitudes where salinity may increase up to 36‰.

Ocean water of the Indian Ocean falling between 0º-10º Latitudes has a salinity of 35.14‰ however it decreases to 30‰ in Bay of Bengal. On the contrary the salinity increases upto 36‰ in the Arabian Sea. This is due to a high rate of evaporation and low humidity. Additionally there is much less fresh water carried to the Arabian Sea by west flowing rivers as compared to Bay of Bengal.

Tides are the rise and fall of sea levels caused by the combined effects of the gravitational forces exerted by the Moon and the Sun, and the rotation of the Earth. The rotation of the Earth creates two forces -
the centripetal
and
centrifugal forces

, which play a major role in the formation of tides. This means that the side of the Earth that faces the Moon experiences a gravitational force, greater than that of the Earth itself. Hence we experience high tides. On the other hand the side of Earth that is facing away from moon experiences less gravitational force from the Moon, as a result, we experience high (indirect high tides) tides. Between these two high tides water level goes down this is called low tides (ebb). Thus in the time span of 24 hrs. and 50 minutes (or 52 minutes) we experience two
High Tides
and two
Low Tides

When the Sun, the Moon and the Earth are aligned in a straight line, we experience a Spring Tide. In astronomy, this situation is known as
syzygy

. It occurs on a full moon or new moon day. On the other hand, when the Sun, the Moon and the Earth are at a right angle to each other the gravitational forces of these celestial bodies act against each other resulting in Neap Tide. Neap Tide is observed on the 7th or 8th day of each lunar month (14 days appx.) During Neap Tides, there is a decrease of 20% in the Spring Tides whereas the Neap Tides are higher than the normal occurrences.
The Moon is the closest celestial body to Earth hence its gravity has a significant impact on our planet. The moon is responsible for the sea waves of the oceans.
The effect of Moon on the tidal forces of our planet is 2.17 times greater than that of the Sun.
The city of Southampton in England experiences 4 tides every day. This occurs because two tides travel from English Channel and two from the North Sea at different intervals.

Oceanic Trenches are long, narrow trenches that plunge to great depths of5000 fathoms or 30000 feet. Trenches account for approximately 7% of the ocean’s relief Contrary to our expectations, most of the deepest trenches are not located in the midst of the ocean; they are more often found close to the continents, particularly in the Pacific Ocean, where several deep trenches have been found.
The Mariana Trench

is the deepest trench in the world. It is located in the Pacific Ocean east of Mariana Islands. The Mariana Trench is a crescent- shaped trough. This trench was discovered in 1875 with the help of a survey ship called HMS Challenger. The Mariana Trench was also surveyed in 1951 by the British survey vessel, HMS Challenger II. The estimated depth of the Challenger Deep in Mariana Trench is 11,033 meters. The prominent trenches of the North Pacific Ocean are - Mariana Trench, Kuril Trench, Aleutian Trench and Japan Trench.

In rivers, erosion, transportation and deposition go on simultaneously from the point of origin to the point where they meet the sea. This process leads to the formation of different terrestrial relief features. Some of them are as follows
Gorge -

It is a deep narrow section of river valley usually with near vertical rock walls, more generally a narrow valley between hills and mountains. Gorges are formed as a result of continued erosion of mountainous terrain by a river. For Ex:
Chisapani Gorge
in Nepal is formed by Karnali River.
Karnali
is the longest river in Nepal (507 km). It is due to the high velocity of the river that it creates many gorges.
Canyon-
Canyons are the more eroded version of gorges.
Grand Canyon
is located in Arizona (US). It is a steep-sided canyon carved by
Colorado River
. The canyon is 446/447 km long with an average width of 6.4 to 29 km and depth of 1.8 km deep.
V-shaped Valley

- V-shaped valleys are formed by erosion. The majority of the rivers in the world carry on two processes simultaneously i.e. vertical and horizontal erosion respectively. These rivers create V-shaped valleys.
Waterfalls-
A waterfall is a stream that falls from a height. Waterfalls are often the sites of the greatest concentration of energy dissipation along the course of a stream.
Meanders-
As water flowing under gravity seldom flows straight for any long distance, a winding course soon appears. The irregularities of the ground force the river to swing in loops, forming meanders.
Alluvial Cones -
Also called alluvial fans, they are cone shaped deposits of sediments built by a stream where it merges into a broad valley or plain.
Delta-

When the river reaches the sea, the fine materials it has not yet dropped are deposited at its mouth, forming a fan-shaped alluvial area called a delta. This alluvial tract is, in fact, a seaward extension of the floodplains. Deltas differ much in size, shape, growth and importance. A number of factors such as the rate of sedimentation the depth of the river, the sea bed and the character of tides, currents and waves greatly influence the eventual formation of deltas. The Ganges Delta is the largest delta in the world. It is also known as Ganges-Brahmaputra, Meghna Delta or Sunderban Delta.

Coral reefs are called the rainforest of the ocean.

Coral reefs are found in abundance in the tropical latitudes i.e. between Tropic of Cancer and the Tropic of Capricorn (generally extending between 30°N to 30°S). They occur in shallow tropical areas where the seawater is clean, clear and warm.
Coral reefs, constitute only about 0.2% of the seafloor, however, they provide for 25% of the oceanic flora and fauna.
Coral is actually a living organism.
When the temperature rises the corals start removing the zooxanthellae from their bodies. As a result, the corals turn white and this phenomenon is called coral bleaching.
Great Barrier Reef

is the largest coral reef in the world. It is located in the Pacific Ocean, North-East of the Australian state of Queensland. The Great Barrier Reef supports extraordinary biodiversity, including more than 450 species of hard coral, 1625 species of fish and over 3000 species of molluscs.
Fringing reefs
are comparatively narrower. This reefsystem lies close to the shore hence, wherever the river meets the ocean the fringing reef breaks. Fringing reefs are found in South Florida, Malaysia, etc.
An
atoll

∗Heavy gases in the atmosphere descend whereas lighter gases are found in the upper layers as they ascend. As a result CO₂ gases extend up to 20 km from the surface, oxygen, and nitrogen up to 100 km, hydrogen up to 125 km and other gases rise far above 125 km except ozone. The atmosphere is made up of different layers of gases with varying densities and temperatures. Based on these factors different layers of the atmosphere are as follows-
(1) Troposphere –

The lowest layer of the atmosphere is called troposphere. All weather activities like clouds, hail, fog, blizzards, thunder, windstorms, etc. are confined to the troposphere. The most important characteristic of the troposphere is that there is a decrease of
with an increase of every 1000 min altitude. This decrease in temperature with an increase in altitude is known as normal lapse rate. The upper boundary of the troposphere is called tropopause.
(2) Stratosphere –

Stratosphere (15-50 km) is the second most important layer of the atmosphere. It lies between mesosphere (above) and troposphere (below). This layer of atmosphere is very dry in nature and has the least amount of water vapor in it. As a result, there is no weather activity in stratosphere. The stratosphere is used for
aviation purposes
as the absence of weather activities makes this layer ideal for flying. Ozone layer is found in this sphere.
(3) Mesosphere –
This layer is found at an altitude of 50 to 80 km. The upper ceiling of mesosphere is called mesopause.
(4) Ionosphere –
It is an electrically conducting layer, that makes
radio wave transmission
possible over long distances. Ionosphere extends from 80 to 640 km.
The unique feature of Ionosphere is the phenomenon of
Aurora Borealis
in Northern Hemisphere and
Aurora Australis
in Southern Hemisphere.
(5) Exosphere
– It is the topmost layer of the atmosphere and is situated above the ionosphere. This layer has
no defined boundary
. The
Communication satellites
are positioned in the exosphere.

∗The only source of energy for the Earth’s atmosphere and its surface is the Sun. The outer layer of the Sun i.e. the photosphere releases energy at a constant rate. As a result, each per unit area of the Earth also receives constant solar energy. This phenomenon is known as the

. ∗ Distribution of Solar Energy – Normally the solar energy received
decreases from
the

However, there are temporal changes in the energy received at every latitude. Since the Sun’s position in comparison to that of the Earth shifts northwards and southwards during Earth’s revolution due to Earth's tilta the maximum solar energy received also shifts north and south of the equator in the same respect. 20° North Latitude receives the maximum solar energy not the equator.
∗Regions where the Sun’s rays fall in a slanted manner receive less solar energy compared to regions where the Sun’s rays are falling vertically.

∗Water vapors are capable ofabsorbing the infrared radiation waves and the outgoing long waves of the dispersed solar waves however, water vapors are transparent to the ultraviolet rays of the sun, hence are incapable ofabsorbing them.

On clouded nights the amount of water vapours in the atmosphere is greater compared to a clear sky night. The outgoing long waves are absorbed by the water vapours present in the atmosphere. Hence, cloudy nights are warmer than clear sky nights.

∗Heat Budget-Energy Balance – the rays of the Sun enter the Earth’s atmosphere as short wave solar radiation and Escape the Earth as long-wave terrestrial radiation. The balance between incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation is known as Heat Budget – Energy Balance.

Long-wave terrestrial radiation plays a major role in keeping the atmosphere warm. The atmosphere is warmed primarily by the difference between incoming solar radiation and outgoing terrestrial radiation. This warmth is captured by gases like carbon dioxide leading to the green house effect and global warming.

A cyclone is a large scale wether system in which winds rotate around a strong center of low atmospheric pressure. Cyclones rotate anticlockwise in the northern hemisphere and clockwise in the southern hemisphere.
Depending on the location cyclones can be categorized into two types – tropical cyclones and temperate cyclones.
(1) Tropical Cyclones
– (Between tropics of Cancer and Capricorn). Tropical cyclones are known by different names in different places. In northern and Northwestern part of Australia they are called
Willy-Willy,
in China, they are called
typhoons,
in the USA they are known as
hurricanes
and in India they are called
cyclones
. In the Great Plains of USA, strong cyclones are formed as a result of Cold polar winds coming in the contact with hot air brought by Gulf streams. These cyclones are called
tornadoes. Tornado Alley
is the name given to the region of the Great Plains affected by Tornados. The places located in the Tornado Alley are –
Mississippi-Missouri Valley, Texas, Oklahoma, Kansas
and
Nebraska.
Tornados are common in the entire tropical and subtropical region but are very prominent in the Caribbean Sea and North America Region.
Fujita scale is used to measure the intensity of tornadoes.
Hurricane is a tropical cyclone affecting the regions of Texas, Mexico, Florida and West Indies.
Saffir Simpson scale
is used to measure potential property damage caused by a hurricane.
Typhoon is also a tropical cyclone that originates in the South China Sea.
Nargis
was a tropical cyclone responsible for heavy destruction in Myanmar.
(2) Temperate Cyclones – These cyclones originate in the mid latitudes.They are often round, building or wedge-shaped. These cyclones are found between
latitudes in both hemispheres. Under the influence of the westerlies blow from west to east.
Anticyclones
have high pressure at their center, around which air circulates.
The pressure decreases from centre towards the outer periphery due to which air blows from the center outwards.
Anticyclones are clockwise in the northern hemisphere and anticlockwise in the southern hemisphere.
The water vapor present in the atmosphere is known as humidity. Humidity is a result of evaporation of water from the earth surface which reaches the atmosphere. Humidity is expressed in two ways –
Absolute Humidity –
it is the amount of humidity present per cubic meter of air at a given temperature.
Relative Humidity –

it is expressed as a percentage. It is a measure of the actual amount of water vapour in the air compared to the total amount of vapour that can exist in the air at its current temperature. Relative Humidity is inversely proportional to the temperature of the air. Humidity decreases from the equator towards poles.
∗Air occupies space and has weight. The atmosphere exerts vertical pressure on the earth’s surface. This is called
atmospheric pressure.
Atmospheric pressure is measured using a barometer. It is measured, as the force exerted per unit area of the barometer. A
sudden fall in the level of barometer
is a sign of an upcoming storm. If the readings of a barometer fall and then start rising slowly it denotes that there will be rainfall.
A continuous
rise in the level of mercury
in the barometer is a sign of an anticyclone and clear weather.
The horizontal distribution of atmospheric pressure is shown by using isobars.
An
isobar
is an imaginary line that connects points having same atmospheric pressure at mean sea level. ∗Based on the process of origin, pressure belts can be divided into two parts-
(1) Based on thermogenesis – pressure belts thus formed are equatorial low-pressure belts and polar high-pressure belts.
(2) Based on motion-pressure belts thus formed are sub tropical high-pressure belts and sub-polar low-pressure belts. ∗
Equatorial Low-Pressure Belts –

The belt extends between 5° north and south of Equator. The equator receives vertical rays of the sun throughout the year. As a result, the air gets heated and starts rising up. Hence the region always experiences low pressure. The surface air of the region moves with very slow velocity as a result of which the environment here is quite calm. This is the reason this pressure belt is also called
Doldrums.
Sub-tropical High-Pressure Belt –

the belt is found between 30°-35° latitudes in both hemispheres. The air rising from the equator starts becoming cooler in the upper layers of atmosphere and hence begins sinking near 30°-35° latitudes. Simultaneously the air from the sub-polar low-pressure belts also starts descending in this region due to Earth's rotation thus a high-pressure zone is created which gives birth to sub tropical high pressure belt. The pressure belt is highly mobile in nature, thus it is also called
Horse Latitude.
Sub-Polar Low-Pressure Belt –

This pressure belt is found between 60°-65° latitudes in both hemispheres. Though the temperature in this region is low throughout the year the region experiences low pressure. This is due to the fact that rotation of the Earth causes the air to spread and displaces it. As a result low pressure is created.
Polar High-Pressure Belts –
The poles and the regions in close proximity to them experience high pressure because the region is very cold which causes the air to become heavy and start descending creating high pressure.

∗ Cloud is a visible dense mass of water droplets or ice crystals suspended in the atmosphere. Hence, collectively clouds are a large version of suspended water bodies or glacial bodies. Clouds are found at a relatively higher altitude compared to fog.
∗Clouds can be categorized depending on their shape, vertical expansion and height.
Cirrus–Clouds –

They clouds are found at the highest altitude. These are fibrous and feathery in appearance as they are made up of tiny ice crystals. When the rays of the sun pass through these ice crystals the cirrus clouds appear white in colour. They are seen before the advent of a cyclone.
Cirro–Stratus Cloud –
They are found at an altitude of 18000 feet and above. Their arrival creates a halo around the Sun and the Moon which is a sign of an upcoming cyclone.
Cirro-Cumulus Clouds –
These clouds are white in appearance and are found in clusters of small ball-shaped patches.
Alto-Stratus Clouds –
These are those high clouds that are spread across the sky as thin sheets of blue and brown clouds. They are responsible for continuous and expanded rainfall.
Alto – Cumulus Clouds
– They are low-level clouds just like cirro-cumulus clouds.
Strato-Cumulus-Clouds
– These are light brown coloured clouds often found in big round shaped patches.
Stratus Clouds –
They are formed as a result of two opposite air bodies, coming into contact with each other. They are often seen during winter in temperate regions.
Nimbo-Stratus Clouds –

They are found close to the surface of the Earth. These grey, often dark clouds are highly dense in nature and can be of any shape. It is because of their highly dense nature that they block the sunlight and make the region dark followed by heavy rainfall.
Cumulus Clouds –
They are highly dense in nature. Their shape is elongated and the upper portion of them resembles a dome or a cauliflower. These clouds are a signal of the start of clear weather.
Cumulo-Nimbus-Clouds –

These clouds are highly diversified and dense in nature. There is a high possibility of rain, hail and thunderstorms associated with these clouds. ∗Thunder is a process of a thunderstorm. In reality, thunderstorms are local storms in which the air ascends with high velocity. Lightning and thunder is witnessed followed by heavy rainfall. Lightning causes a sudden and high increase in the temperature of the air leading to a sudden expansion in the air which result in thunder.
The movement of air as a result of the difference in horizontal air pressure is known as
wind

. Wind in general flows from a high- pressure area to a low-pressure area. If the earth were still and flat, the winds would blow from a high-pressure area directly to a low-pressure area along the isobaric lines at an angle of 90o. However, the Earth is geoid in shape and rotates on its own axis. Hence winds under the influence of dynamic forces keep shifting their trajectory.
Types of Winds
– There are basically three types of wind
Planetary Winds –
Winds blowing constantly in a particular direction throughout the year are called planetary winds. The main planetary winds are –
trade winds, westerlies
and
polar easterlies
Trade winds are winds blowing from sub tropical high-pressure belts toward equatorial low-pressure belts in both the hemispheres.
Westerlies-

They blow from sub-tropical high-pressure belts (30°-35°) toward sub-polar low-pressure belts (60°-65°) in both the hemisphere. Since there is more landmass in Northern Hemisphere compared to Southern Hemisphere the westerlies in the former case are more complex, and they are less influential in summers as compared to winter.

Due to the presence of less landmass in the Southern Hemisphere the westerlies travel at such a high speed causes them to become stormy. It is because of this high intensity of the westerlies in the southern hemisphere that around 40° latitudes they are known as
Roaring
Forties, around 50° latitude they are called
Furious Fifties
and around 60° latitude they are called
Shrieking Sixties
Wellington (New Zealand) is the only capital in the world that lies in the path of Roaring Forties.
Polar winds
blow from polar high-pressure belt to
sub-polar low-pressure
belt.
Periodic winds
– Winds are those that reverse their direction as per season or time. The important periodic winds are – monsoonal winds, land and sea breezes, breezes of mountains and valleys.
Monsoonal winds
are those that completely reverse their direction according to seasons. During the six months of summer they blow from sea to land and during the six month of winter they blow from land to sea.
Land and Sea Breezes

only cover 20 to 30 km of the area including the coastal area. During daytime the land heats up faster than the nearby sea as a result low pressure is created over land and thus cool and moist winds blow from sea to land. This wind is called a
sea breeze
. There is a complete reversal in the direction of the wind during the night. As a result, winds blow from land to sea. This wind is called
Land breeze
Mountain and Valley Breeze -
During daytime the air heats up and rises along the slope of the mountain. This is known as
Valley Breeze
(Anabatic flow). During the night the air gets cooler and heavier as a result it starts descending along the slope of the mountain. This is known as
Mountain Breeze
(Katabatic flow).
(3) Local Winds –
These winds are generated as a result of regional differences in temperature or air pressure. Hence, they affect a very small area.

∗The Mediterranean Sea is located between 30° to 40° North Latitudes. Hence, the sea comes under the influence of the sub-tropical high-pressure belt. This belt is mobile in nature. During summers, the trade winds blow in these latitudes and in winter these latitudes come under the influence of westerlies. This means that the westerlies blow towards North east from this region and Trade Winds blow towards south west from this region.
Local winds are generated as a result of pressure and temperature gradient in a particular region and hence affect a very small area. These winds are confined to the lower level of the troposphere.
Important local winds are as Follows:
Chinook

means snow-eater. These winds descend along the eastern slope of the Rocky Mountains and are warm and dry in nature. These winds increase the temperature of the region during winters resulting in the melting of snow and the emergence of fresh greenery in the region. The winds rising along the southern slope of Alps descend along the northern slope and are warm and dry in nature. It is called

in Europe and has its maximum influence in Switzerland.

is a local wind prevailing in Southern California. It is also a warm and dry wind like Chinook but unlike Chinook, it blows as a Channel Wind in the valley east to west.

is a local wind that blows in a northeast and east direction in the western parts of Sahara Desert. It is also dry and dusty air. With the advent of Harmattan, the weather becomes dry, pleasant and healthy. It is the reason why Harmattan is also called

in the coastal areas of Guinea.

is a local wind that blows from the Sahara Desert towards the Mediterranean Sea. The wind is dry, warm and sandy in nature. This air contains a lot of red sand. . The sand carried by Sirocco from Libya is transported to Malta, Italy, Spain, Croatia, Montenegro, Albania and Greece.

is a local wind that blows in the deserts of Arabia and Kurdistan.

is a cold polar wind that blows around the northwestern part of the Roum Sea, affecting the areas of Spain and France.

is a dry cold air that moves at a very fast pace. It prevails along the eastern coasts of Adriatic Sea. The northern part of Italy is highly influenced by Bora.
Loo
is a dry and hot local wind that prevails in northern India. It blows from northwest and west to the east. These winds are tropical and dry and travel at a high velocity.
Norwesters
are pre monsoon thunderstorms blowing in India which are also known as
Kalbaisakhi
Zonda
is a warm dry wind that blows along the eastern slopes of the Andes Mountains and influences the country of Argentina.
Black Roller
is a local wind prevailing in the Great Plains region of North America.
Purga
is a cold local wind prevailing in the tundras of Russia.
Levanter
is a cold local wind that blows from east to west in Spain.
Pampero
is a local northwestern cold wind of the Pampas region of South America.

Climate is the average weather in a place over a certain period of time. It is determined by the daily weather conditions of a place (like temperature, rainfall, winds, humidity, air pressure etc) persisting over a long duration of time.
Earth has been basically divided into three climatic zones –
Tropical Zone, Temperate Zone
and
Frigid Zone
. These zones extend from the equatorial region towards poles.

The continent of Asia extends from equatorial region to North Pole. As a result, all types of climates are found here. Different climates are found in different parts of the world. Places having same climates are called climatic regions and they are as follows:
Equatorial Climatic Region

– Found in between 0° to 10° North and South of the equator. The temperature remains high in this region all throughout the year. As a result, the region remains humid and it receives rainfall in the afternoon. The flora of the region consists of broadleaf evergreen trees like Gutta Percha, Rubber, Ebony, Palm, Bamboo, Bet, Mahogany, Sandal, Cinchona, etc. The regions under this climate include
– Amazon Basin, the Congo Basin of Africa, Guinea Coast, Eastern island groups, and eastern Central American (Panama, Costa Rica, Nicaragua, Honduras, Guatemala).
Tropical Monsoonal Climatic Region
– The region lies in the route of trade winds. Places included in this region are –
India, Bangladesh, Myanmar, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Eastern Coastal Regions of Africa, South-Eastern coastal parts of USA and northern parts of Australia
etc.
Sahara Type of Climatic Region
– Also known as a
tropical dry desert type

of climate. The climate extends between 15° to 30° latitudes on both sides of the equator in the western parts of the continent. There are two distinct seasons in this type of climate, the summer season and the winter season. Seasons are distinguished based on temperature. The average temperature of the summers is between 30°-35°C. According to the readings of NASA’s satellite (2003-2009)
Dasht-e-Lut
desert of Iran was the hottest place on the planet based on surface temperature. Highest recorded temperature in 2005 was 70.7°C. Places under Sahara type of climate includes –
Thar desert and Arabian Peninsula of Asia, Sahara and Kalahari deserts of Africa, Western deserts of Australia, Atacama desert of South America and Western desert of North America.
Savanna type of climatic region –

the temperature of the equatorial type of climate and savanna type of climate are some what the same. Since the savanna type of climate lies between the equatorial type of climate and tropical desert climate, the region is dominated by grasslands. The savanna type of climate is also called
Sudan type
of climate. There is a distinct dry and moist season however the temperature is high throughout the year. The places included in this region are – V
enezuela, Colombia, Guyana, South-Central Brazil,
and
Paraguay
. The maximum extent of savanna type of climate in Africa is found in Sudan and northern region of Australia.
Mediterrannean Type of Climatic Region:

Also known as sub-tropical dry summer type of climate. Since this type of climate is found near the Mediterranean Sea it is known as Mediterranean Climate. Mediterranean type of climate is found between 30° to 40° latitudes in both the hemispheres on the western parts of the continents. Maximum rainfall occurs in winter. Summers are dry and winters are wet. The summer winds are dry in nature. The places included under the Mediterranean type of climate are – river valleys of France, southern Italy, Greece, western Turkiye, western Israel, and North Western Africa which includes Algeria, Southern California of North America, Central Chile, and south-western part of South Africa.

– This type of climate is found in the temperate grassland regions. This type of climate is found in the middle latitudes in the central parts of the continent. grasslands of USA
and
Canada, grasslands of South Australia
and
Eurasia

– Found between 40° to 65° latitudes in both the hemispheres in the western part of the continents. The average temperature is between 15°-21°C. North Western Europe, Western Norway, Denmark, North Western Germany, France, Oregon and Washington in the USA, British Columbia in Canada, Chile
and
New Zealand

– It is a moist continental type of climate, found on the eastern ends of the continent, predominantly in the Northern Hemisphere between
latitudes. There is a good amount of rainfall throughout the year but more in summer as compared to winter. The places included under St. Lawrence type of climate are –
Manchuria region
of China,
St. Lawrence Valley
of North America and the coastal provinces of Canada.

– Also known as a Siberian type of climate which comes under microthermal climate. The winters are long and the summers are of short duration. , from

and

climatic
and

play a vital role in the formation of soil. The color, formation and minerals of the soil depend upon the
bedrock

contribute to the formation of the soil and also increase its productivity. Hence, they are known as

. Earthworms create pores in the soil, allowing the percolation of air and water and release of carbon dioxide.

in the soil.

(2) Illuviation – Different salts are introduced from the upper horizon to lower due to percolation of water.
(3) Capillary Action – It is responsible for upward movement of water from wet areas to dry areas of the soil. The smaller the pore the higher the capillary action and vice versa.
The capillary function is highest
clay soil
and lowest in
sandy soils
. The effectiveness of capillary action in four different soils is as follows –
Clay
Loam
Sandy soil

soil is found in grassland and transitional areas. It is mostly found in a temperate steppe climate and is also found in humid grasslands.

is a process through which the top layer of soil along with nutrients is eroded from one place to another.

is a method used to conserve soil in hilly areas. During rainfall, it prevents the soil from washing away. Under Contour Banding terrace like structures are made on the slopes of the hilly areas which prevent the soil from washing away with the downfllow of water.
