Vegetation growing well in rock terrain are called
Lithophytes
, vegetation growing well in tropical deserts are called
Xerophytes
and vegetation growing well in swamps and marshes is called
Hygrophytes
. Hydrophytes are aquatic plants.

chapters.title: The Major Tribes of the World
chapters.group: The Major Tribes of the World

runs: Tribal peoples are those groups of people who are similar to each other on the basis of social customs, language and culture.
Nomadic Tribes

are those groups of people that travel from one place to another to find fodder for their cattle. Though nomadic tribes are found all over the world, they are mostly concentrated in arid regions. They are primarily found in the arid regions of
Africa
Central Asia
, and
South America
When people shift from one location to another in a particular season and then return to the same location after that season is over, it is called
seasonal migration
For example when it starts to snow in the mountains the tribal people shift to the valley and return after the winter season is over.
Gaddi
Bakarwal
and
Bhotia
are some of the tribes of India that practice seasonal migration.
Pygmy Tribe
is found in the rainforests of
Congo
Basin in Equatorial Africa. They are hunters and gatherers. They construct huts at the tops of trees which are called
Mongulu
. They are black short- statured people of Negrito race.
Eskimo tribes
are found in the
tundra regions of Alaska
Canada
and
Greenland
. They are of Mongoloid race and hunting is their main occupation. They use a weapon called the
harpoon
and a
Yayak boat
to catch fish.
Inuit
is a cultural group of indigenous people found in Arctic regions of Canada, Greenland (Denmark), Russia and Alaska.
Maasai tribes
are found in the plateau regions of
East Africa
which include Kenya, northern Tanzania and eastern Uganda. They are cattle herders and their main occupation is cattle rearing. They live in huts called
Kraal
Bushman Tribe

is found in desert regions of Kalahari which include South Africa, Zimbabwe, Eswatini, Botswana, Namibia, etc Hunting and gathering is their main occupation. They are omnivorous. Termites are called the rice of Bushman.
Zulu tribes

reside in South Africa. They are known for their culture and rituals. The Battle of Isandlwana was fought between the British and Zulu tribe in 1879. The tribe practices agriculture and cattle rearing.
Semang tribe
resides on the island of Malay in Malaysia. They belong to
Negrito race
and depend on hunting and gathering.
Sakai tribe
is found in the forests of the Malay Peninsula, Malaysia and Indonesia. They use blowpipes for hunting.
Papua tribes
reside in Papua New Guinea (Pacific Ocean). They practice agriculture and cattle rearing.
The
Sami tribe
(Lapps tribe) is found in Norway, Sweden, Finland and the Kola Peninsula in Russia. The region is also known as
Fenno Scandinavia

Bedouin tribes are found in the desert regions of Arabia, especially in the northern part of Saudi Arabia. Living in tribal groups they practice a migratory lifestyle. They belong to Armenoids and Mediterranean (Caucasian) races.
The
Bora tribe
is found in the coastal areas of Western Amazon Basin, Brazil, Peru and Colombia. They practice primitive agriculture and are known to be cruel in nature.
Kirghiz tribe

is a group in Central Asia spread between Pamir Plateau in Kyrgyzstan and the Tianshan mountain range. Kirghiz tribes are cattle rearing tribes that practice seasonal migration. They build round shaped temporary tents known as
Yurts
Yupik tribe
is found in Eastern Russia and Western Alaska. The tribe uses sledges (ice carts driven by dogs).
Yukaghir
is a Mongoloid tribe found in Verkhoyansk (North-East Siberia) and Stanovoy Mountains.
Maya tribe
is found in Central America, mainly in Mexico, Guatemala and Honduras.
Maori
is a Polynesian tribe residing in New Zealand. Their main occupation is agriculture and gathering.
Among the other tribes of the world –
Fulani tribes
reside in West Africa,
Bantu tribe
resides in eastern, southern and central Africa,
Nuba tribe
resides in Sudan,
Vedda tribe
is found in Sri Lanka,
Barber tribe
resides in Morocco and north Africa
Enu tribe
resides in Japan and
Aeta tribe
is found in the Philippines.
Important tribes of India are – Oran, Gond, Kol, Santhal, Bheel and Toda.
India is believed to be the indigenous place of the
Gypsy
. The Gypsy people are believed to be associated with dome Caste (Scheduled Caste) of India.
Archaeopteryx
was the first bird to emerge on Earth somewhere around 150 million years ago.
Africa is believed to be the birthplace of Mankind. At present,
Caucasian race

is counted amongthe largest races on Earth. They have straight or curly hairs, dark blue or brown eyes and a cranial Index of80 and above. Hobble and Elliot Smith have categorized Caucasians in to three groups
Nordic, Alpine
and
Mediterranean.
Caucasians
are the largest group in the world.
Mongoloid race
is mostly found in
Central
and
Eastern Asia
. They have yellowish and brown skin and a small forehead.
Negroids
are dark brown to brown in appearance. Africa is their indigenous place.
Cro-Magnon

is believed to be the most modern of the human species. It existed up to the emergence of the present modern man i.e. Homo sapiens. The first evidence of Cro-Magnon was found in an excavation in France in Dordogne Valley in 1868. It is believed that Cro Magnon dates from the Upper Paleolithic Period (40000 to 10000 years ago).

The Linguistic Census has two important parts – (A)L-1 is the population associated with primary language or mother tongue, and (B)L-2 is the population associated with not only the mother tongue but also with a second language as well. The combined population of
and
is the total population of people speaking a particular language.
Top 20 Most Spoken Languages, 2026
Hindi 611.2 Million
Spanish 561.3 Million
Standard Arabic 334.9 Million
French 333.5 Million
Bengali 274.4 Million
Portuguese 269.4 Million
Indonesia 254.8 Million
Urdu 246.0 Million
Russian 210.3 Million
Standard German 133.4 Million
Japanese 125.7 Million
Nigerian Pidgin 120.7 Million
Egyptian Arabic 118.4 Million
Marathi 99.2 Million
Vietnamese 97.1 Million
Telugu 95.9 Million
Swahili 95.2 Million
Hausa 94.5 Million
According to Ethnologue English is the most spoken language as per L-1. According to this figure, Hindi is the 3rd most spoken mother tongue after English and Mandarin.

Esperanto is a language designed to assist in international communications. Though it is not an official language of any country yet around 10-20 lakh people use it. In the neighboring countries of India, Urdu is spoken in Pakistan and Burmese in Myanmar.
The official languages of Mauritius are English and French. Apart from them, Hindi, Urdu, Hakka, Bhojpuri, Creole, etc are also spoken.
The official language of Singapore are Malay (National), Tamil, English and Mandarin.
The official language of Chile, Colombia and Cuba is Spanish.
A. Agriculture & Livestock
Grains are the main source of food for humankind. The important grains are Rice, Wheat, Corn, Millet, Barley, Chickpea, and Pulses etc.

Rice is cultivated in tropical, semitropical and temperate regions. Hence rice is grown in most of the wet humid areas of the world, although it can be grown in arid regions also with the help of irrigation. In most areas around the world, rice is grown as a Kharif crop, which is harvested in Nov.-Dec., but in Java, it is harvested in April-May. The
International Rice Gene Bank
, maintained by I
nternational Rice Research Institute (IRRI)

is located in Los Banos (Philippines). IRRI was established in the year 1960. Paddy is very famous in China. Out of the total area under rice cultivation in China halfis used to cultivate hybrid rice.

According to FAO, 2024 India has the maximum area under rice cultivation (50.51 million hectare) followed by China (29.26 million hectare). Despite having less area under rice cultivation, China has a total area under irrigation whereas in India only half of the area under rice cultivation is irrigated. According to Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) 2024 the four leading producers of rice in the world are - 1. India (217.87 million tonnes), 2. China (207.53 million tonnes), 3. Bangladesh (60.57 million tonnes), 4. Indonesia (53.14 million tonnes) and 5. Vietnam (43.45 million tonnes).
According to latest updates – from FAO 2024,
Tajikistan
has the largest productivity of rice (13385.8 kg/ha) followed by
Australia
Wheat

is basically a temperate crop. Its cultivation spreads up to 60° latitudes in Northern Hemisphere and up to 40° latitudes in Southern Hemisphere. Wheat requires an average temperature of 10°C during germination and an average temperature between 15°-20°C during the development of grains. A Timely rainfall between 20 cm and 70 cm is also required.
According to FAO, 2024 the top
four leading producers of wheat
in the world are – China (140.10 million tonnes), India (113.29 million tonnes), Russia (82.59 million tonnes) and the USA (53.65 million tonnes).
Sugarcane
requires a tropical as well as
subtropical climate
where the average temperature is between 21°C-27°C with average rainfall between 75 cm 150 cm. According to FAO 2024, the
top five leading producers of sugarcane
in the world are – 1. Brazil (759.66 million tonnes), 2. India (453.16 million tonnes), 3. China (102.09 million tonnes), 4. Pakistan (84.24 million tonnes), 5. Thailand (82.44 million tonnes).
Sugar beet

is a plant of temperate climate.According to FAO 2024 the two largest producers of sugar beet in the world are Russia and the Germany. Russia and the Germany are followed by France, USA and Turkiye. In Ukraine, the entire production of sugar is from sugar beet.
Cotton

is a tropical and subtropical plant. Quality and type of cotton are determined by the length of the fibers, shine, etc. According to FAO 2023 the top 5 leading producers of cottonseed in the world are – 1. India (10.60 million tonnes), 2. China (9.40 million tonnes), 3. Brazil (4.49 million tonnes), 4. USA (3.31 million tonnes), 5. Pakistan (3.17 million tonnes), while the top 5 leading producers in terms of cotton lint are (FAO 2023)
– 1. China (5.62 million tonnes), 2. India (5.53 million tonnes),
3. Brazil (2.92 million tonnes) 4. USA (2.63 million tonnes),
5. Pakistan (1.74 million tonnes).
According to FAO 2024, India is the largest producer of
castor oil Seed
. India produces
1.59 million tonnes of castor oilseeds. India is followed by Mozambique (0.07 million tonnes), Brazil (0.03 million tonnes).
According to FAO 2024, the
top 5 leading producers of bananas
in the world are – India (37.61 million tonnes), China (11.76 million tonnes), Indonesia (9.26 million tonnes), Ecuador (7.56 million tonnes) and Brazil (7.05 million tonnes).
According to FAO 2024, the
top 4 leading producers of coconut
(shell) in the world are – 1. Indonesia (17.99 million tonnes), 2. India (14.71 million tonnes), 3. Philippines (14.50 million tonnes) and 4. Brazil (3.16 million tonnes).
Tobacco
cultivation requires high temperatures. It grows well between 21° to 27°C. Tobacco requires an annual average rainfall of100 to 120 centimeters. According to FAO 2024, the
leading producers of tobacco

(unmanufacture) in the world are – (1) China (2.26 million tonnes), (2) India (0.73 million tonnes), (3) Brazil (0.64 million tonnes), (4) Indonesia (0.53 million tonnes) and (5) Zimbabwe (0.24 million tonnes).
Rubber
is obtained from the
latex
of a tree found in the equatorial evergreen forests. Rubber trees are tropical trees that require a temperature of
to
and an average annual rainfall of 150 to 200 cm. According to FAO 2024, the
top 5 leading producers of natural rubber
in the world are – 1. Thailand (4789.04 thousand tonnes), 2. Indonesia (2262.09 thousand tonnes), 3. Cote d'Ivoire (1686.59 thousand tonnes),
4. Vietnam (1327.47 thousand tonnes) and 5. China (877.60 thousand tonnes).
Coffee is a bush type of tree found in the tropical and subtropical regions. The
Abyssinian Plateau
(Ethiopia) is the native place of coffee. The main species of coffee are – (1)
Coffea Arabica

– It occupies 3/4 of the total coffee in the world. (2) Coffea Robusta – Grown on a large scale in Africa, in countries such as Ethiopia and Uganda. Robusta is grown in India.According to FAO 2024, the
leading producers of green coffee

in the world are – 1. Brazil (3387.72 thousand tonnes), 2. Vietnam (2015.29 thousand tonnes), 3. Colombia (839.85 thousand tonnes), 4. Indonesia (807.58 thousand tonnes), 5. Ethiopia (575.69 thousand tonnes), 6. Uganda (402.00 thousand tonnes), 7. India (363.00 thousand tonnes).
Tea

is a plant of the tropical and subtropical regions but can also be grown in the hilly areas of the temperate zones. Tea requires a long summer with an average temperature between 20°-30°C. Tea also requires average rainfall between 130 and 150 cm.

According to FAO 2024 China produces the maximum tea leaves (16260.90 thousand tonnes) in the world followed by India (6156.03 thousand tonnes), Kenya (2687.20 thousand tonnes), Sri Lanka (1514.02 thousand tonnes) and Turkiye (1414.00 thousand tonnes).
Tea was first used in China as a
medicinal drink

. Maize is the third most important grain after rice and wheat. It is native to Latin America. In Western cultures (mainly the U.S.A.), Maize is used as fodder for animals while in Latin America, it is consumed by people as food source. According to FAO 2024, the
top 5
leading producer of
Maize
(corn) in world are –
1. USA
(377632.69 thousand tonnes),
2. China
(294920.00 thousand tonnes),
3. Brazil
(114953.30 thousand tonnes),
4. Argentina
(57494.50 thousand tonnes),
5. India
(40230.57 thousand tonnes).
Plantation agriculture
is mostly practiced in tropical regions. It is practiced on small pieces of land rather than in large estates. Every region has some specific crop growing in that place.
According to the Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare plantation crops include
Coconut, Cocoa, Arecanut
and
Chashew nuts
. However according to Ministry of Commerce and Industry plantation crops include –
Tea
Coffee, Rubber
and
Spices
. Hence, plantation agriculture includes – Coconut, Arecanut, Cocoa, Cashew nut, Tea, Coffee, Rubber and Spices.
Horticulture includes
Pomology
(Cultivation of Fruits),
Olericulture
(cultivation of Vegetables) and
Floriculture

(Cultivation of Flowers). Now, Mushrooms, Bamboo, Spices etc. have also been brought under the definition of Horticulture. Horticulture requires a lot of manual labor. Coffee cultivation is a horticultural practice in Hawaii (USA). The coffee of Hawaii is famously known as
Kona coffee. Mocha coffee
is produced in Yemen. Mocha is the name of the harbor from where it is imported.

The diverse climate of India ensures the production of a variety of vegetables and fruits. According to FAO, 2024 India is the largest producer of fruit (other fruit, n.e.c.), and second largest producer of vegetables (other vegetables, fresh n.e.c.) after China.
In
alley cropping
, crops are grown in the spaces left between the trees planted in rows.
Taungya
is a type of shifting agriculture practised in Myanmar.
Chena
jhuming
and
milpa
are also associated with shifting agriculture.
The regions of Europe close to the Mediterranean Sea are famous for the
cultivation of grapes
. Around 85% of the total grapes produced are used for making wines.
Sacramento-San Joaquin Valley
is located in California (USA). Sacramento is a flat/internal valley, the where River San Joaquin creates an inland delta. The valley is world famous for grapes and citrus fruit.
Golden Crescent is the name given to the countries that produce and export
poppy
. Countries included in the Golden Crescent are Pakistan, Iran and Afghanistan.

Groundnuts are native to Brazil, Mato Grosso and its nearby areas. Groundnut is the main crop of Gambia and has a major role to play in the country’s GDP (Gross Domestic Product). According to FAO, 2024 China is the largest producer of groundnuts excluding shelled in the world.
Catechu (kattha)

is obtained from the wood of Acacia catechu tree. First time in the world, American agronomist Norman Borlaug developed the high yielding variety (HYV) seeds in Mexico. According to the International Agreement on Agriculture, a
Green Box
is an instrument through which economic assistance is provided in the fields of– research related to control of insects and disease, training, general awareness, marketing and promotion activities.
Shahtoosh
is a special woolen shawl made out of the hairs of Tibetan Antelope and Chiru.
Chiru

is found in the Chinese Autonomous Region of Tibet. Earlier it was also found in western Nepal. Chiru is also found in the union territory of Ladakh. Apiculture is associated with the rearing of honey bees for honey production.
Viticulture
is associated with study and production of grapes.
According to FAO, 2023 China is the largest producer of
raw silk
in the world, followed by India. Other countries producing silk include Uzbekistan, Vietnam, Democratic People's Republic of Korea and Brazil.

Nitrogen is an essential element for the development of plants. It is important for the development of plant cells and tissues hence a deficiency of nitrogen hampers the growth of plants causing the leaves to turn yellowish in colour and dry up. Rhizobium, Azotobacter, Azospirillum and blue-green algae are used as bio-fertilizers for crops.
Blue-green algae

is used as a bio-fertilizer in paddy fields, whereas azotobacter is used as a bio-fertilizer for paddy wheat, maize, mustard, potato, cotton etc. Azospirillum is used as a bio-fertilizer for Paddy, Sorghum, Millet, Sugarcane, Maize etc.
Alfa-Alfa is a flowering plant of the Fabaceae pea family. It is cultivated as an important fodder crop. In the United Kingdom, Australia, South Africa and New Zealand, it is called Lucerne grass.
Animal husbandry is more developed in those regions where natural grazing lands or grasslands are found in abundance. The credit for commercializing animal husbandry is given to European migrants.
Ranches

are large farms for cattle grazing. They are built by enclosing natural grasslands with barbed wire and then using them as grazing lands for livestock. Maximum livestocks is found in Asia. According to FAO 2020, the
countries with maximum livestock population are

– China (829.58 million), India (545.33 million), Brazil (304.15 million), and USA (201.69 million). Western Europe, USA, Canada, Russia, Australia and New Zealand are important regions of dairy farming. According to the Basic Animal Husbandry Statistics, 2025 milk production in the country (India) continues to increase as it is anticipated to be 247.87 million tonnes in 2024-25 with a per capita availability of milk at about 485 grams/day. According to World Food and Agriculture Statistical Yearbook, 2025 the top five leading producers (2023) of milk (bovine milk) in the world are – India (231.49 million tonnes), USA (102.68 million tonnes), Pakistan (62.54 million tonnes), China (45.71 million tonnes), and Brazil (36.44 million tonnes).
(i) Coal

When small pieces of rock collect below the surface, it leads to the formation of sedimentary rock also known as layered rocks. Fossils and fossil fuels are found in the sedimentary rocks. Sedimentary rocks occupy 75% of the total Earth's surface.
Minerals such as coal, slate, marble, salt (rock), petroleum are found in sedimentary rocks. Coal and limestone are examples of sedimentary rocks ofbiotic origin.
Based on the percentage of carbon present coal is categorized into four types–
(1) Anthracite
- It is the best quality of coal having a carbon content of 90%–95%.
(2) Bituminous
– It is next to Anthracite in terms of quality having a carbon content of 70% to 90%.
(3) Lignite
- Famously known as brown coal having a carbon content of 45%–50%. It is mostly used in thermal power plants.
(4) Peat
–It is low-grade coal having a carbon content of 40% or less.
Rock coal
is also known as Anthracite. It is the highest quality of coal.

According to data from World Mineral Production 2019-2023 in the year 2023, China produced more than half of the world's production of coal. The top three leading producers (2022) of coal in the world are – (1) China, (2) India, (3) Indonesia. The top 5 countries in terms reserves of coal in the world by the end of year 2023 are USA, Russia, China, Australia and India respectively.
The
North Appalachian
coal area is the largest coal area in the USA. The region produces the best quality of coal. The other important coal regions of USA are –
South Appalachian
Western Interior coal region
and the coal region of Rocky Mountains etc.
Ruhr is a river that flows through Germany. The Ruhr Valley is the main coal region and industrial area known as
Ruhr
Basin.
Saarland is located on the borders of France and Germany in the
Saar River valley
. This area is said to have huge deposits of coal.
Donets Basin
, also known as Donbass is currently located in Ukraine. It is an important coal producing region.
Provinces of Shaanxi and Sichuan in China are important coal producing areas. Kuznets Basin of Russia and Lancashire in the U.K. are also famous for coal production.

The most abundant metal found in Earth's core is iron. It is found along with Aluminium, Lime, Magnesia, Soapstone, Titanium, Arsenic, Copper, Phosphorus and other minerals. With the Industrial Revolution picking up pace the extraction of Iron also gained momentum.

According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23, the top five leading producers of iron ore in the world (in the year 2023) are –1. Australia (952.51 million metric tonnes), 2. Brazil (436.84 million metric tonnes), 3. India (277.96 million metric tonnes), 4. China (250.00 million metric tonnes), 5. Russia (90.80 million metric tonnes).
According to the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026 top five leading countries in the world in terms of iron content reserves are–(1) Australia (2) Brazil (3) Russia (4) Mauritania (5) India.
The
Krivoy Rog region
of Ukraine and Magnitogorsk in Russia are famous for iron ore production.
The
Pilbara region
and
Hamersley
mine area of Australia are famous for iron ore extraction.
In USA large scale production of iron ore is done in
Minnesota and Michigan.
Copper is the most important metal after Iron in the field of industries.
Huge reserves of copper are found on the western slope of Andes Mountains, ranging from northern Peru to central Chile.
According to World Mineral Production 2019- 23 in the year 2023
Chile
is the largest producer of copper ore.
Huge
deposits of porphyry copper are found in the mountainous region of Andes. The
Chuquicamata copper

mine in northern Chile is located in this region. These copper deposits are believed to be of post Eocene, Oligocene epoch. Copper was first produced in the USA in the Keweenaw Peninsula of the state of Michigan. Apart from this copper was also produced in the Butte region of Montana in the USA.
The largest copper producing area of Canada is
Sudbury
(Ontario). Also, the Canadian regions of
Flin Flon
and
Britannia Beach
are famous for copper production. Katanga province of Democratic Republic of the Congo is known for copper mining. It is located near the border of Zambia.

Zambia is a landlocked country in Africa. There is a long copper (reserve) belt from Zambia to Katanga (D. R. Congo). Though this belt has large deposits of copper, the lack of marine transport dilutes the possibilities of trading and export of the region's copper.
Japan is self-sufficient in copper production. The production of copper in Japan is more than its consumption.
The top Five leading countries in terms of copper reserves are –
Chile, Australia, Peru, Russia/Congo,
and
Mexico.
According to the figures of World Mineral Production 2019- 23 the top five leading countries in terms of copper production (in 2023) are–(1)
Chile
Democratic Republic of the Congo
Peru
China
and
(5) USA.
Gold is obtained from two sources. In natural form, it is are found in the layers of quartz rocks as rock gold it is also found as small granules in placer deposits of rivers.
According to the figures of Indian Minerals Yearbook, 2024,
Australia
has the largest gold reserve. The province boasts of two of the world famous gold mines–the
Coolgardie
and
Kalgoorlie
. Gold is being extracted from Mount Morgan in Australia. The important gold deposits of USA are found in South Dakota, Black Hills,
Salt Lake, Alaska and the Yuba region of California.
In Canada, gold is being extracted from the provinces of
Quebec
and
Ontario
Important gold producing areas of China are Yunnan, Manchuria and Tsingling Shan.
Important gold producing areas of South Africa are
Johannesburg
Mponeng
Boxberg
, etc. It is famous for the extraction of gold and diamonds.
According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23 the largest producers of gold (In 2023) are–(1)
China
Russia,
Australia
Canada
According to USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026 the top three leading countries in the world in terms of gold reserves are–Australia, Russia and South Africa.

Silver is the second most precious metal after gold and is used for making ornaments, coins, electroplating, photography and medicinal purposes. It is found in free elemental form in nature in metamorphic rocks, 2026.

According to figures from the USGS Mineral Commodity Summaries, 2026. The top four countries with the largest silver reserves are–Peru (110000 tonnes), Russia (92,000 tonnes), Australia (91000 tonnes), China (67000 tonnes), Poland (59000 tonnes).
According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23. The top five countries in terms of silver (metal content) production (2023) are– Mexico, China, Peru, Poland and Russia.
German silver
is also known as, nickel silver, paktong, new silver, alpacca, etc. It is an alloy comprised of
60% copper, 20% zinc
and
20% nickel

(However according to NCERT the composition of German silver is Cu (25-30%), Zn (25-30%) and Ni (40-50%). Hence, the alloy does not contain any silver. Since it shines like silver it was given the name German silver.
Aluminium is a whitish colored metal. Bauxite is the ore of aluminium.
According to World Mineral Production 2019-23, in the year 2023, the top five leading countries in terms of aluminium (primary) production were–
China, Russia, India, Canada and UAE.
The
Cape York
Peninsula and
Weipa region
of
Australia
, the
Saline County of Arkansas
(USA), the
Cola Peninsula
of the Russia are some important regions of the world where Bauxite production is being done.

About 80% of the world's tin is found in placer deposits. These deposits are located in riverbeds and Valleys or on the sea floor. Maximum placer deposits are spread across South East Asia. Most of the tin deposits in China are found in the plateau region of Yunnan.
In Indonesia tin is produced from the
Sumatra islands

of Bangka and Belitung. In Malaysia, tin is produced from the Kinta Valley (Perak province), Kuala Lumpur, and Pahang province. In South America, tin deposits are found in the eastern Andes region, within a belt.
According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23 as per the figures of the year 2023, the top five leading producers of tin (mine production) in the world are –
China
(66500 tonnes),
Indonesia
(50669 tonnes),
Myanmar
(47081 tonnes),
Peru
(26230 tonnes) and Brazil (25121 tonnes).

Petroleum is a liquid, formed as a result of different mixtures ofhydrocarbons. Petroleum is a multicolored substance. The multicolours are due to the mixture of different chemicals present in it. Petroleum is found in sedimentary rocks. It gets accumulates in the stoma and interstices of porous sandstones and limestones.

The first commercial oil well was drilled in Romania in 1857. Romania is the first country in the world whose crude oil production has an official document (1857 AD. 275 tonnes) and was recorded at the international level. However according to the Ministry of Petroleum & Natural Gas, GOI Edwin L. Drake drilled the worlds first oil well in 1859 at Titusville, Pennsylvania, U.S.A. According to Indian Minerals Year Book 2022, the largest share of reserves of world crude oil is available in Middle East (48.3%), followed by South & Central America (18.7%), North America (14%), CIS (8.4%), Africa (7.2%), Asia Pacific (2.6%) and Europe (0.8%).
According to World Population Review data in 2024, the top three leading countries in terms of crude oil proved reserves are –
Venezuela
(303.2 Billion Barrels),
Saudi Arabia
(267.2 Billion Barrels) and
Iran
(208.6 Billion Barrels).
According to World Mineral Production, 2019-23 (data 2023) the largest crude oil producers in the world are –
USA
(874.11 million tonnes),
Russia
(541.70 million tonnes),
Saudi Arabia
(531.70 million tonnes),
Canada
(277.90 million tonnes),
Iran
(214.30 million tonnes).
The important petroleum producing countries in Asia are – Saudi Arabia, Iran, Iraq, UAE, Kuwait, Oman, Qatar etc.
The largest oil-producing country in South-East Asia is
Indonesia
. Sumatra, Java, Kalimantan are the important oil producing regions of
Indonesia
. In China oil is produced in Sichuan, Shanxi, Yumen and Saidum which lie in the North-Western part. Crude oil is produced in 32 U.S. states and in U.S. coastal waters.
In
Canada
petroleum is produced in Alberta province (Leduc region), Manitoba and British Columbia.
In the former Soviet Union petroleum was produced in the
Volga-Ural region
Baku region
(Azerbaijan) and regions lying in proximity the Caspian Sea. The country of
Venezuela
in South America is an important oil-producing country in the world. Petroleum exports constitute more than 80% (2025)
of the total exports of Venezuela
. Large scale production of petroleum is done in Brazil and Colombia. Normally mineral oil is found in those places where other fossil fuels are found. It is also found independently in some places.
According to the data of Statistical Review of World Energy 2025, the top five leading countries in terms of natural gas reserves are – (1)
Russia
Iran
Qatar
USA
and (5)
Saudi Arabia
The top five leading producers of natural gas in the world (2023) are – (1)
USA
Russia
Iran
China
Qatar
Gasohol
is usually
90% Gasoline

These rivers maintain flow throughout the year; therefore, they are called perennial rivers. A major reason is that the highest Himalayan range—Greater Himalaya/Himadri—and the Trans-Himalayan ranges remain largely snow-covered throughout the year, and many glaciers originate from these ranges. Snow and glacier melt provide continuous water supply even in summer, while rainfall (especially monsoon rainfall) adds additional water.

Thus, both (A) and (R) are correct, and (R) directly explains (A), because the presence of high, snow-covered ranges and associated glaciers plays a decisive role (as a major reason) in sustaining the perennial nature of Himalayan rivers.

stem: The flat plains along the sub-Himalayan region in North India, are called –

runs: The flat plains along the sub-Himalayan region in North India, are called Bhabar. It is a narrow belt only 8 to 16 kms in width and lying parallel to the Shiwalik foothills at the break-up of the slope. This zone is studded with pebbles and it consists of porous beds which have been laid down by the numerous streams as they descend down the hills. The porosity is so high that all streams lose themselves in the Bhabar. South of the Bhabar is the Tarai belt, with an approximate width of15-30 km where most of the streams and rivers re-emerge without having any properly demarcated channel, thereby, creating marshy and swampy conditions known as the Tarai. This has a luxurious growth of natural vegetation and houses a varied wildlife.

Many longitudinal thrusts and faults lie in the Himalayas. The Main Frontal Thrust (MFT) lies when moving from south to north. Above this is the extension of Greater Himalayas, which is also known as the CCZ (Central Crystalline Zone). HHC (Higher Himalayan Crystalline) is located above the MCT Tibet Himalaya is situated between HHC and STDS (South Tibetan Detachment System). The Himalaya lies to the north of ITSA Due to the location of the reverse region and the Himalayan geographical structure, it becomes the most concentrated earthquake zone in India. stem: Consider the following statements about Peninsular plateau.

runs: 1. Rising from the height of 150 m above the river plains up to an elevation of 600-900 m is the irregular triangle known as the Peninsular plateau.

Peninsular Plateau Rising from a height of 150 m above the river plains upto an elevation of 600-900 m is the irregular triangle known as the peninsular plateau. Delhi ridge in the northwest, (extension of the Aravalis), the Rajmahal hills in the east, Gir range in the west and the Cardamom hills in the south consitute the outer extent of the Peninsular plateau. However, an extension of this is also seen in the northeast, in the form of Shillong and Karbi - Anglong plateau. The peninsular India is made up of a series of patland Plateaus such as the Hazaribagh plateau, the Palamu plateau, the Ranchi plateau, the Malwa plateau, the Coimbatore plateau and the Karnataka pleteau etc. This is one of the oldest and the most stable landmasses of India.
The general elevation of the plateau is from the west to the east, which is also provend by the pattern of flow of rivers.

Delhi ridge in the northwest (extension of Aravalis), the Rajmahal hills in the east, Gir range in the west and the Cardamom hills in the south constitute the outer extent of the Peninsular Plateau. The height of this plateau generally decreases from West to East. So statements (1) and (3) are incorrect.

stem: 'Moribund Delta' is a sub-division of which of the following Delta?

runs: "Moribund Delta" is a sub-division of Bengal Delta. The Moribund delta areas are in the southwestern part of the Bangladesh, south of the Ganges river, where tributaries are highly silted and are profusion of oxbow lakes. Such areas are Jessore, Kushtia and Faridpur. The immature delta is to the south of the Moribund delta and mainly consists of sea beaches and tidally influenced lands. The Sundarbans belong to this region. The mature delta part is more towards the central part of the southern section of Bangladesh. The active delta is situated mainly at the delta of the Meghna River entering the Bay of Bengal. Regular flooding and the formation of"chars" and "offshore islands' are its characteristics.

stem: Which of the following is the actual source of Son river?

runs: Two states– MP and Chhattisgarh have own claims and counterclaims regarding the origin of the Son River.
The website of Anuppur district (M.P.) mentions that the origin of Son river is at a place called Sonmuda, located in Anuppur.

In 1952-53, the then President Rajendra Prasad was shown the origin of the Son river at Sonmuda in Amarkantak (hill). Because of this reason, Sonmuda (Anuppur District, formerly part of Shahdol district) gained popularity and obtained public recognition as a place of origin of the Son river in various published sources.

Chhattisgarh recognizes that the flow of Sonmuda from Anuppur joins the Arpa river via Amanala, Amadob Nala, and Mati Nala. Arpa joins the Mahanadi via Shivnath. According to Chhattisgarh, the actual origin of the Son river
is Sonbachharwar village of Gaurela-Pendra-Marwahi

district (formerly part of Bilaspur district) of Chhattisgarh. Factual details are available in support of Sonbachharwar in Authentic maps of the Sidhi District Gazetteer Survey of India (published during joint state of Madhya Pradesh and Chhattisgarh), the Archaeological Survey of India, 19th century A.D. and the book 'Son Ke Pani Ka Rang' by Dev Kumar Mishra.

According to the India Water Resources Information Systems of the Ministry of Jal Shakti, Government of India, the source of Son River is located on the Amarkantak hill of Maikal mountain range in Chhattisgarh.

According to the Envis Centre of the Ministry of Environment, too, the origin of Son River is in Pendra Road Tehsil. Presently this tehsil is located in Gaurela-Pendra Marwahi district of Chhattisgarh.

See lines mentioned in the District Census Handbook Bilaspur published by the Office of the Registrar General and Census Commissioner, Government of India - According to saying, Son river originates from Amarkantak, but according to Geologists, this river originates from Sonekund, about 19 km. southeast of Pendra Road in Chhattisgarh.

In fact, confusion originates also arises due to the fact that in both places, the origin of Son river is shown in the kund (pool). After this, the river flows underground. From the surface, the Son river flows from the village of 'Cholna' in Anuppur district.
According to mythology, Son (male) and Narmada (female) are like lovers, and the origin of rivers of this type cannot be very close, i.e., from the same place.
The rivers originating from the same place are in the form of brother and sister. Even if we view it from this perspective, the origin of Son seems to be inclined in favor of Chhattisgarh.
What do aspirants do?
If the options as the source of Son are the Maikal mountain range or Amarkantak hill, then there is no problem as both the sites are situated on Amarkantak hill of Maikal mountain range.
If the option remains only Anuppur or only Sonbachharwar, then there is no problem as both places are recognized as the place of origin.

If both places are given in the options, first of all, it has to be seen in which state exam this question has been asked. If the question is asked in MP then answer must be Anuppur, and if the questions asked in Chhattisgarh, then the place of Chhattisgarh will have to be selected as the place of origin.

The language of the question also matters. For example there is the above question which is asked in U.P. P.C.S. but stated to be the 'original' place of origin. That is why the answer to this question has been considered as Son Bachharwar of Chhattisgarh.
It is also true that if the origin of the Son in Chhattisgarh is recognized, the number of states, districts and areas increases where Son river flows.

stem: Which one of the following Indian rivers forms an estuary?

runs: An estuary is a partly enclosed coastal body of water with one or more rivers or streams flowing into it, and with free access to the open sea. Estuaries form a transition zone between river environments and ocean environments and are subject to both marine influences, such as tides, waves, and the influx of saline water; and riverine influences, such as the flow of freshwater and sediments. The inflow of both seawater and freshwater provides high levels of nutrients in both the water column and sediment, making estuaries among the most productive natural habitats in the world. The St. Lawrence River makes the world's largest estuary, while the Narmada and Tapti (Tapi) make India's largest estuary.

stem: Compare the Himalayan river with the Peninsular river based on the following comparisons:

runs: 1. Most of the Himalayan rivers are perennial, whereas most of the Peninsular rivers are rain fed.

3. The Peninsular river causes more erosion on its way in comparison to the Himalayan river.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

e: None of the above / More than one of the above

runs: The rivers of the Himalayan region rise in glaciers, are perennial. The Peninsular rivers do not have their sources in glaciers, and most of them are rain-fed. The gradient of the Himalayan river is steeper than that of the Peninsular river as the slopes of the Himalayan rivers are very steep in the upper reaches. That is one reason they erode and transport huge amounts of sediment. Further, the landforms over which these rivers flow are also young. On the other hand, the peninsular rivers do not have very steep gradient and they flow on already eroded old topography. Further, more the hard rocks of the Peninsular region are not as susceptible to erosion as those of the Himalayan region.

stem: Which of the following statements is not correct?

b: El Nino weakens the Indian Monsoon.
d: La Nina strengthens the Indian Monsoon.

runs: El Nino appears as a warm oceanic current near the coast of Peru in the eastern and central tropical Pacific Ocean. El Nino generally has an adverse effect on India's Southwest Monsoon, often leading to drought like conditions. The El Nino phenomenon occurs irregularly at intervals of approximately two to seven years.

La Nina is the condition opposite of an El Nino. In a La Nina the tropical Pacific trade winds become very strong and an abnormal accumulation of cold water occurs in the central and eastern Pacific Ocean.

stem: What are true in relation to jet stream?

runs: 1. Jet stream blow across Asian Continent at latitudes North of Himalayas parallel to Tibetan highlands.
2. Tibetan highland divides jet stream into North and South Branches.
3. The northern branch of jet stream plays important role in winter weather in India.

During the winter, a distinct pattern of air circulation is observed higher up in the atmosphere. Significantly, westerly winds continue to affect western and central Asia extending approx. 9 to 13 km from west to east. At latitudes north of the Himalayas and almost parallel to the Tibetan highlands, these winds blow across the Asian continent. Thus the first statement is true.

Notably, these jet streams are obstructed by the hills of Tibet consequently, jet stream splits in two. One of its branches flows north of the Tibetan highlands and the other, which originates south of the Himalayas, blows eastward before merging again to form a single stream over China, Hence statement 2 is correct.
Notably, the northern branch of jet stream does not play an important role in winter weather in India. So statement (3) is false.

Zone V covers 10.9% of the area of the country with the highest risk suffering earthquakes of intensity MSK IX or greater. The IS code assigns a zone factor of 0.36 for Zone V. Structural designers use this factor for the earthquake resistant design of structures in Zone V. The zone factor of

0.36 is indicative of effective (zero period) level earthquake in this zone. It is referred to as the very high damage risk zone. The regions of J & K (UT), Ladakh (UT), Some parts of Uttarakhand and Bihar, the North-East Indian region and the Rann of Kutch fall in this zone.
Zone IV:

This zone is called the High Damage Risk Zone and covers the area liable to MSK VIII. The IS code assigns a zone factor of 0.24 for Zone IV. The Indo-Gangetic basin and the capital of the country (Delhi) as well as the rest of the Himalayas is included in Zone IV. In Maharashtra, the Patan area (Koyananagar) is also in Zone IV. This zone covers the remaining parts of Himachal Pradesh, Sikkim, the northern parts of Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal, parts of Gujarat and small portions of Maharashtra near the west coast and Rajasthan. It comprises 17.3% of the areas of the country.
Zone III:
The IS code assigns a zone factor of 0.16 for Zone III. It covers the Lakshadweep islands. This zone is a classified as Moderate Damage Risk Zone. It includes 30.4% of the areas of the country.
Zone II:

The IS code assigns a zone factor of0.10 (maximum horizontal acceleration that can be experienced by a structure in this zone is 10% of gravitational acceleration) for zone II. It comprises 41.4 % of the areas of the country.
Major parts of the peninsular region and Karnataka Plateau fall in this Zone. Thus, it does not come under the zone of high seismic intensity.

stem: What is the factor of Tropical cyclone in the month of May?

The most important factor for the tropical cyclone in the month of May is local temperature variation. stem: Identify the correct order of the process of soil-erosion from the following:

a: Splash erosion, Sheet erosion, Rill erosion, Gully erosion
b: Sheet erosion, Splash erosion, Gully erosion, Rill erosion,
c: Rill erosion, Gully erosion, Sheet erosion, Splash erosion
d: Gully erosion, Rill erosion, Sheet erosion, Splash erosion

runs: The correct order of the process of soil erosion is given below:
i. Raindrop or Splash erosion:
Erosion preceded by the destruction of the crumb structure due to the impact of falling raindrops on the surface of the soil is termed as splash erosion.
ii. Sheet erosion:

It is the fairly uniform removal of soil in thin layers from the land surface, often scarcely perceptible, especially when caused by wind. Areas where loose, shallow topsoil overlies compact soil are most susceptible to sheet erosion.
iii. Rill erosion:
A form of water erosion in which numerous very small and more or less straight channels are produced; the channels get obliterated by ordinary use. It can be removed by normal tillage operations.
iv. Gully erosion:
A form of water erosion in which gullies are produced by a combination of unattended rills.
v. Stream channel erosion:
Stream banks are eroded by water either flowing over the sides of a stream or scouring at the base. It is aggravated by the removal of vegetation, overgrazing, or cultivation near the stream banks.

The destruction of soil cover is described as soil erosion. The soil forming processes and the erosional processes of running water and wind go on simultaneously. Deforestation is one of the major causes of soil erosion. Plants keep soils bound in locks of roots and thus prevent erosion. Terrace farming is a method of soil conservation. The tropical climate is not responsible for soil erosion.

runs: Assertion (A): In the Himalayan mountains different types of vegetation are found.
Reason (R): In Himalayas, there are variations in climate with change in altitude.
Select the correct answer from the code given below:
Code:

a: Both (A) and (R) are true, but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A).
d: Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).

runs: The diversity of vegetation in the Himalayas is clearly due to climatic variations with increasing altitude. As altitude increases, temperature gradually decreases; the pattern of humidity and rainfall/snowfall changes; and due to slope and aspect, sunlight and shade conditions, as well as moisture availability, also differ. This creates successive bioclimatic belts. In the lower regions—Terai-Bhabar and the Shivaliks— tropical moist deciduous forests (e.g., sal) are found; at middle elevations, subtropical/temperate forests (chir pine, banj/oak, deodar and fir) occur; above that, sub-alpine conifers are seen; and in the highest parts, alpine grasslands and shrubs are found.

Above the tree line, tundra-like vegetation occurs, while above the snow line (permanent snow), no permanent vegetation is found. In the Eastern Himalayas, due to higher humidity, evergreen and dense forests occur, whereas in rain-shadow areas (Trans-Himalaya), dry shrub vegetation is found.
Thus, (A) is true and (R) is also true; moreover, (R) correctly explains (A). In other words, variation in climate with altitude is the fundamental reason for vegetation diversity in the Himalayas.

stem: The maximum irrigation potential of India is created through:

runs: Irrigation projects in India are classified into three categories:
1. Minor Irrigation Projects:

All groundwater and surface water schemes that have a Culturable Command Area (CCA) up to 2,000 hectares individually are classified as Minor Irrigation Schemes. The minor irrigation projects comprise all groundwater development schemes such as dug wells, private shallow tubewells, deep public tubewells, and boring and deepening of dug wells, and small surface water development works such as storage tanks, lift irrigation projects, etc. 62 percent of the irrigation potential of India is created through minor irrigation projects.
2. Medium Irrigation Projects:
Those having a CCA of more than 2,000 hectares to 10,000 hectares fall under the category of medium irrigation projects.
3. Major Irrigation Projects:

Irrigation projects having a Culturable Command Area (CCA) of more than 10,000 hectares each are classified as major projects. 38 percent of the irrigation potential of India is created through major and medium irrigation projects.

runs: In the upper part of the troposphere or at the tropopause, generally at an altitude to 5 to 9 miles (approximately 8 km to 15 km.), a powerful circumferential wind current flowing from west to east in a broad belt spanning hundreds of kilometes is know as the jet stream. The discovery (confirmed) of the jet stream occured during world war II, although atmospheric scientists had proposed the existence of jet streams before that. The wind speed in jet streams varies seasonally, becoming stronger in winter compared to summer. The wind speed in these streams typically range from 129 to 225 km/h, but it can exceed 443 km/h. Therefore, the flow speed of jet streams can be considered to range between 300 and 500 km/h. Hence, (A) is incorrect, but (R) is correct.

stem: How is permaculture farming different from conventional chemical farming?

runs: 1. Permaculture farming discourages monocultural practices but in conventional chemical farming, monoculture practices are pre-dominant.
2. Conventional chemical farming can cause increase in soil salinity but the occurrence of such phenomenon is not observed in permaculture farming.
3. Conventional chemical farming is easily possible in semi-arid regions but permaculture farming is not so easily possible in such regions.
4. Practice ofmulching is very important in permaculture farming but not necessarily so in conventional chemical farming.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

The method of agriculture that makes more use of the resources of nature without misusing or polluting it can be called sustainable agriculture. In this, agriculture is done by adopting soil water and naturally made manure and for its conservation, crop rotation, covering the soil under mulching method, etc. So statement 1, 2, 4 are true. This method is effective even in dry semi-arid regions, so statements 3 is false.

stem: What is/are the advantage/advantages of zero tillage in agriculture?

runs: 1. Sowing of wheat is possible without burning the residue of previous crop.
2. Without the need for nursery of rice saplings, direct planting of paddy seeds in the wet soil is possible.
3. Carbon sequestration in the soil is possible.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Zero tillage is the process where the crop seed will be sown directly through drillers without prior land preparation and thus avoiding disturbing the soil where previous crop stubbles are present.

Zero tillage and direct seeded rice (DSR) not only enable sowing of wheat without any burning of crop residue, but also save water by doing away with transplanting operations in paddy. Zero tillage is environmentally safe reducing greenhouse effect by way of carbon sequestration.

stem: What are the advantages offertigation in agriculture?

runs: 1. Controlling the alkalinity of irrigation water is possible.
2. Efficient application of Rock Phosphate and all other phosphatic fertilizers is possible.
3. Increased availability of nutrients to plants is posible.
4. Reduction in the leaching of chemical nutrients is possible.
Select the correct answer using the code given below:
Fertigation is a method of fertilizer application in which fertilizer is dissolved into the irrigation water through the drip system.

Urea, potash and highly water soluble fertilizers are available for use through fertigation. Use of super phosphorus through fertigation must be avoided as it results in precipitation of phosphate salts. Thus, second statement is not correct and the correct answer is (c).

stem: In the context of India, which of the following is/ are considered to be practice(s) of eco-friendly agriculture?

runs: 1. Crop diversification
2. Legume intensification

4. Vertical farming
Select the correct answer using the code given below:

Crop diversification: It refers to the adoption of diverse new crops to the existing cropping pattern, consistent with the ago-climatic conditions of the area besides the ground water conditions. It helps in moving away from nonculture and water-guzzling crops characterinzing agriculture practices in India.
Legume (they fix the atmospheric nitrogen) intensification is an eco-friendly agricultural practice.
Tensiometers (a sealed, water-filled tube with a ceramic porous cup and a vaccum gauge at the top) could be really helpful in providing estimates of soil moisture, thus helping in water conservation.
Vertical farming: Crops are grown indoors, under artificial conditions of light and temperature. It uses significantly reduced water and pesticides than in traditional agriculture.

Conservation agriculture is a method that keep agricultural cost low. High profits and sustainable product can be brought. Along with this, there is a balanced increase in natural resources like soil, water, environment, and biological factors. In this, there is a balanced and proper use of agricultural chemicals and inorganic and organic sources along with agricultural activities such as zero tillage/minimum tillage, so that there is no adverse effect on the various bio-functions of agriculture. In conservation agriculture, minimum tillage allows crop residues to remain on the soil surface. This greatly reduces soil erosion. Generally it is very important to keep the soil covered by crop residues up to 30 percent. It is very important to adopt crop diversification and crop rotation in protected cultivation.Generally, farmers follow the same type of crop rotation for many years. For example, farmers have been planting the paddy wheat cropping system in the same field for years, which directly affected the fertility of the soil. It does impact crop diversification maintains soil fertility and reduces crop related pests and diseases.

stem: In which months is the Rabi crop sown?

runs: On the basis of seasons, the crops in India have been divided into three types.
Kharif crops:
The Kharif crop is the summer crop or monsoon crop in India. Kharif crops are usually sown with the beginning of the first rains i.e in June- July and harvested in October - November.
Major Kharifcrops of India include Millets (Bajra & Jowar), Cotton, Soyabean, Sugarcane, Turmeric, Paddy (Rice), Maize, Moong (Pulses), Groundnut, Red Chillies, etc.
Rabi Crops:

The Rabi crop is the spring harvest or winter crop in India. It is sown in October-November last and harvested in March-April every year. Major Rabi crops in India include Wheat, Barley, Mustard, Sesame, Peas, Potatoes.
Zaid Crop:
This crop is grown in some parts of the country from March to July. Prominent examples are Muskmelon, Watermelon, Vegetables of Cucurbitaceae family such as bitter gourd, pumpkin, ridged gourd, etc.

Coalbed Methane and Shale Gas are unconventional sources of energy. Coalbed Methane is 90% more pure methane gas extracted from the coal seam. stem: Consider the following statement:

runs: 1. Natural gas occurs in the Gondwana belts.
2. Mica occurs in abundance in Kodarma.
3. Dharwars are famous for petroleum.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?

Petroleum and natural gas are found in the sedimentary rocks of the tertiary plate. Gondwana belts belong to the upper Palaeozoic and Mesozoic periods and the Dharwar rocks belong to the late Archean period. Both these rocks are of a much older period and consist mostly of metamorphosed rocks and thus are very poor in petroleum and natural gases. Hence, both statements 1 and 3 are incorrect. Kodarma lies in Jharkhand and is quite famous for its mica. That is why it is called as the 'Mica City of India'. Thus, only statement 2 is correct and the right answer is option (b).

stem: In which of the following industries is rock phosphate used?

runs: Rock phosphate is primarily used in the fertilizer industry. It is a major source of phosphorus, which is an essential nutrient for plant growth. Rock phosphate is used to produce phosphate fertilizers such as single super phosphate (SSP) and di-ammonium phosphate (DAP). Phosphorus is one of the three primary nutrients for plants (nitrogen, phosphorus and Potassium) and therefore plays a crucial role in enhancing crop yield in the agricultural sector.

stem: Consider the following statements:

3. The Narwapahar Mine is operated by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
The details are as follows:

(1) Petronet LNG Ltd. is an Indian oil and gas company formed by the government of India to import liquefied natural gas (LNG) and set up LNG terminals in the country. It is a joint venture company promoted by the Gas Authority of India Limited (GAIL), Oil and Natural Gas Corporation Limited (ONGC) and Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) with an authorized capital. Petronet LNG Ltd has set up its first LNG terminal at Dahej in Gujarat with a capacity of 17.5 million metric tonnes per year. Another terminal with a capacity of 5 million tonnes per year was commissioned in Kochi (Kerala).

(2) The Head Office of the Dredging Corporation of India is strategically located on the eastern seaboard of India at Visakhapatnam. DCI helps to ensure the continuous availability of the desired depths in shipping channels of the major and minor ports, Navy, fishing harbors and other maritime organizations. The horizons of dredging activities are fast expanding worldwide, and its services are increasing in demand and are put to use in the areas of environmental protection, tourism, flood control, irrigation, power generation, port development, mining, laying of offshore pipelines and so on.
(3) The Narwapahar Mine is the a trackless uranium mine located in Jharkhand which is being operated by the Uranium Corporation of India Limited.

Which of the above are included in the World Heritage List of UNESCO?

All four sites are included in the World Heritage List of UNESCO. Champaner- Pavagarh Archaeological Park is located in Panchmahal district of Gujarat. A concentration of largely unexcavated archaeological, historic and living cultural heritage properties cradle in an impressive landscape that includes prehistoric (chalcolithic) sites, a hill fortress of an early Hindu capital, and remains of the 16th century capital of the state of Gujarat. It was included in the World Heritage List of UNESCO in the year 2004.

The Chhatrapati Shivaji Terminus, formerly known as Victoria Terminus Station, in Mumbai, is an outstanding example of Victorian Gothic Revival architecture in India, blended with themes derivied from Indian traditional architecture. The building, designed by the British architect F. W. Stevens, became the symbol of Bombay as the 'Gothic City' and the major international mercantile port of India. The terminal was built in 10 years, starting in 1878.

Mamallapuram, also known as Mahabalipuram, is a tourist town 60 km south of Chennai famous for its stone carvings. The structures here mostly carved straight out of granite, are among the oldest existing examples of Dravidian (South Indian) architecture. It was included in the World Heritage List of UNESCO in 1984 due to its unique elegance. Konark Sun Temple is a 13th-century Sun Temple on the west coast in Odisha, India. The temple was built by King Narasimha Deva I. The temple has been constructed in the form of a giant ornamented chariot of the Sun God, Surya with seven horses and 24 wheels. It was included in the world heritage List of UNESCO in 1984.

stem: The “Big Bang Theory” is related to –

stem: The milky way is classified as –

The galaxy in which our solar system is situated is known as the ‘Milky Way’. Asteroids are generally considered to be made up of metals and rocky material, while comets are made up of ice, dust and rocky material. Asteroids are found much closer to the Sun. stem: The tail of comet is directed away from the Sun, because–

b: As the Comet rotates, the lighter mass of the Comet is attracted by some stars situated in the direction of its tail.
c: The radiation emitted by the Sun exerts a radial pressure on the comet throwing its tail away from the Sun.
d: The Tail of the Comet always exists in the same orientation.

runs: In the outer solar system, comets remain frozen and are extremely difficult or impossible to detect from Earth due to their small size. As a comet approaches the inner solar system, solar radiation causes the volatile material within the comet to vaporize the steam out of the nucleus, carrying the dust away with it. The streams of dust and gas thus released form a huge, extremely tenuous atmosphere around the comet called the coma and the force exerted on the coma by the Sun's radiation pressure causes an enormous tail to form, which points away from the Sun. Hence (c) is the correct answer.

stem: A ship is moving from the eastern side of Aleutian Islands towards Dutch Harbour. It crosses 180° meridian on 1st January 1999 at 23:30 hr. What time and date will be recorded by the captain of the ship in his diary after one-hour journey from the point of crossing of the meridian?

stem: On June 21 every year, which of the following latitude(s) experience(s) a sunlight of more than 12 hours?

On June 21 every year, among the given latitudes, the Tropic of Cancer and the Arctic Circle (as these are in Northern Hemisphere) experience a sunlight of more than 12 hours. On 21st June, the Northern Hemisphere is tilted towards the Sun. The rays of the Sun fall directly on the Tropic of Cancer. As a result, these areas receive more heat. The areas near the poles receive less heat as the rays of the Sun are slanting. The North Pole is inclined towards the Sun and the places beyond the Arctic Circle experience continuous daylight for about six months. Since a large portion of the Northern Hemisphere is getting more light from the Sun, it is summer in the regions north of the equator. The longest day and the shortest night at these places occur on around 21st June. This position of the Earth in Northern Hemisphere is called the Summer Solstice. At this time in the Southern Hemisphere all these conditions are reversed. It is winter season there. The nights are longer than the days.

stem: Consider the following statements:

runs: Over the past several hundred years, the position of the Earth’s rotation axis has shifted slightly, and the length of the day has increased by a very small but measurable amount. Therefore, Statement I is correct. Solar flares and the often-associated coronal mass ejections (CMEs) indeed deliver a large amount of energy to the Earth’s outermost atmosphere (mainly the upper ionosphere/thermosphere and the magnetosphere). However, this energy largely remains confined to the upper atmosphere and the magnetosphere; its effect on the Earth’s mass distribution or on the solid body of the Earth is generally not a primary driver compared with large-scale mass redistribution Process. Due to the melting of Greenland, Antarctica, and other ice sheets, the solid ice mass reaches the oceans in the form of water. Thus, both

Statement II and Statement III are factually correct. Only Statement III provides the scientific explanation for the changes occurring in the Earth’s rotation and axis (Statement I). Statement II merely describes the impact of solar flares on the upper atmosphere, not the shift of the Earth’s axis.

runs: Chemical weathering is the process that breaks down rock through chemical changes. Rainfall and temperature can affect the rate at which rocks weather. Rainwater may contain impurities from the atmosphere in the form of dust particles and dissolved gases like oxygen, nitrogen and carbon dioxide.

When water (e.g. rainwater) mixes with carbon dioxide gas in the air or in air pockets in soil, a weak acid solution, called carbonic acid, is produced. When carbonic acid flows through the cracks of some rocks, it chemically reacts with the rock causing some of it to dissolve. This process is called carbonation. It is very active in limestone regions.

Rainwater contains dissolved oxygen from the atmosphere, which can participate in oxidation processes that contribute to weathering. Oxygen in rainwater reacts with minerals, particularly iron-bearing ones, to form oxides or rust, leading to weakening and breakdown.

stem: During an earthquake, which type of waves get generated?

e: F.S.L.

runs: The seismic waves are generated in three forms. (1) P- (Primary) Waves – these waves travel fastest. (2) S - (Secondary) Waves- these waves cause particles to oscillate. Both P and S waves are called ‘Body waves’because they can travel through the interior of the Earth. (3) Surface Waves – these waves arrive after P and S waves and are confined to the surface of the Earth during an earthquake. There are two types of surface waves (i) Love waves and (ii) Rayleigh waves.

stem: Read the following statement related to 'Earthquake shadow zone' and choose the correct option:

runs: Statement I: The shadow zone of one earthquake is totally different from the shadow zone of another earthquake
Statement II: Seismometers record both 'P' and 'S' waves at any distance out of 105º from earthquake's epicentre

a: Statement I and Statement II both are true
b: Statement I is true, but Statement II is false
c: Statement I is false, but Statement II is true
d: Statement I and Statement II both are false

runs: Earthquake waves get recorded in seismographs. However, there exist some specific areas where the waves are not reported. Such a zone is called the 'Shadowzone'. The study of different events reveals that for each earthquake, there exists an altogether different shadow zone.

P waves don't arrive between 105° (103° - 105°) and 140° due to refraction at the mantle-core boundary, however S waves don't reappear beyond an angular distance of ~ 130° as they are stopped by the liquid outer core.

stem: Consider the following statements:

runs: 1. The Richter scale is a logarithmic scale and so an increase of 1 magnitude unit represents a factor of 10 in amplitude.
2. Each integer reading of the Richter scale has an energy 100 times that the previous integer reading.
Which of the statement(s) given above is/are correct?

The magnitude of the earthquake is measured on the Richter scale and intensity on the Mercalli scale. In 1935, seismologist Charles Francis Richter of the California Institute of Technology developed the Richter magnitude scale. It is based on a logarithmic scale whose base is 10. Each number on the seismogram represents 10 times amplitude and 32 times energy release. A seismic wave of magnitude 1 releases the energy of 6 ounces of TNT. Hence statement
(1) is correct while statement (2) is wrong.

stem: Consider the following statement about earthquake –

4. Every integer on Richter Scale shows a 100 times increase in energy released

The intensity of an earthquake is measured by the Mercalli scale. Hence, statement (1) is correct. The magnitude of an earthquake is the measurement of energy released, thus statement (2) is correct. The Richter scale has a shaking amplitude 10 times that of the previous integer and shows an increase of 32 times in energy release. There are three types of mountains - Fold Mountains, Block Mountains and Volcanic Mountains. The Himalayan mountains (Asia), the Andes (South America) and the Alps (Europe) are young fold mountains with rugged relief and high conical peaks. The Aravali range in India is one of the oldest fold mountain systems in the world. The range has considerably worn down due to the processes of erosion. The Appalachians in North America and the Ural mountains in Russia have rounded features and low elevation. They are very old fold mountains.

Block mountains are created when large areas are broken and displaced vertically. The uplifted blocks are termed as horsts and the lowered blocks are called graben. The Rhine valley and the Vosges mountains in Europe are examples of such mountain systems.
Volcanic mountains are formed due to volcanic activity. Mt. Kilimanjaro in Africa and Mt. Fujiyama in Japan are examples of such mountains.
Hence, rows 1 and 2 are not correctly matched while rows 3 and 4 are correctly matched.

stem: Epeirogenic forces are result of:

runs: The forces that cause physical and chemical changes on Earth's surface are known as geomorphic processes. All changes occur under the influence of certain forces that continuously act within the Earth as well as on its surface. Forces acting on the Earth's surface are called exogenic forces, while those operating inside the Earth are termed endogenic forces. Among the endogenic forces, epeirogenic forces cause uplift and emergence due to upward movement in large parts of the Earth's crust and subsidence and sinking due to downward movement. stem: Consider the following statements:

The Red Sea is a sea inlet of the Indian Ocean, lying between Africa and Asia. Its connection to the ocean is in the south, through the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait and the Gulf of Aden. The Red Sea region receives very little precipitation in any form, although prehistoric artifacts indicate that there were periods with greater amounts of rainfall. No water enters the Red Sea from rivers, and rainfall is scant; but the evaporation loss–in excess of80 inches per year–is made up by an inflow through the eastern channel of the Bab-el-Mandeb Strait from the Gulf of Aden. The Red Sea is one of the saltiest bodies of water in the world, owing to high evaporation and low precipitation; no significant rivers or streams drain into the sea, and its southern connection to the GulfofAden, an arm of the Indian Ocean, is narrow. Hence, both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

stem: Which one of the following currents does not contribute to forming a complete circle of currents in the South Atlantic Ocean:

runs: In the South Atlantic Ocean, there exists a fixed order of complete circular currents. This order emerges from South Equatorial Current. After hitting the Brazilian coast, it moves south towards where it is called Brazil current. The disturbance developes due to the rotation of the Earth. At 40° latitude, this current is affected by west wind. It turns east and current coming from the south i.e, Falklands Current meets the Brazil Current. stem: What are the causes of high-tide low tide formation in the oceans?

a: Due to the effect of the sun
b: Due to the rotation of the Earth
c: Due to the combined effect of sun and the moon
d: Due to Gravitation, Centripetal force and the centrifugal force

runs: High tide/low tide occur as a result of the gravitational pull between the Earth and the Moon alongwith the two forces namely centripetal force and centrifugal force acting upon the Earth. Ocean water is kept at equal levels around the planet by the Earth's gravity pulling inward, but Moon's gravitational force is strong enough to disrupt this balance by accelerating the water in the hemisphere that faces the Moon. When the Moon's force of attraction is stronger than the centrifugal force of the Earth, causes high tides to occur. On the other hand, when the centrifugal force is stronger than the Moon's force of attraction indirect (high tides) occur. Between these two high tides water level decreases which is called low tides (ebb). Earth experiences high and low tides twice in 24 hours and 50 minutes.

stem: Formation of delta is affected by:

runs: Conditions that are favorable for the formation of deltas are as follows:
The river must carry a large amount of sediment.
The slope and speed of the river must not be strong enough to remove the sediments deposited by the river.
The slope of the sea floor or lake at the river mouth must be gentle or flat.
The large size and volume of the river.
Presence of a shallow adjoining sea or continental shelf. Thus, a
river delta

is a landform that forms at the mouth of a river, where the river flows into an ocean, sea, lake, or reservoir. Deltas form with the deposition of sediments carried by a river. Over long periods, this deposition builds the characteristic geographic pattern of a river delta. Thus option (d) is the most probable answer.

stem: Which of the following is/are correct inference/ inferences from isothermal maps in the month of January?

The temperature distribution is generally shown on the map with the help of isotherms. The isotherms are lines on the map joining places having equal temperature. In general the effect of latitude on temperature is well pronounced on the map, as the isotherms are generally parallel to the latitude. The deviation from this general trend is more pronounced in January than in July, especially in the Northern Hemisphere. In the Northern Hemisphere the land surface area is much larger than in the Southern Hemisphere. Hence, the effects of land mass and the ocean currents are well pronounced. In January the isotherms deviate to the north over the ocean and to the south over the continent. This can be seen in the North Atlantic Ocean. The presence of warm ocean currents, such as the Gulf Stream and North Atlantic Drift, makes the Northern Atlantic Ocean warmer and the isotherms bend towards the north. Over the land the temperature decreases sharply and the isotherms bend towards south in Europe. Hence, inference 1 is correct while inference 2 is incorrect.

stem: With reference to "Coriolis force", which of the following statements is/are correct?

runs: 1. It increases with increase in wind velocity.
2. It is maximum at the poles and is absent at the equator.
Select the answer using the code given below:

The rotation of the Earth about its axis affects the direction of the wind. This force is called the Coriolis force after the French Mathematician who described it in 1844. It deflects the wind to the right in the northern hemisphere and to the left in the southern hemisphere. The deflection is greater when the wind velocity is high, that means Coriolis force increases with an increase in wind velocity. The Coriolis force is directly proportional to the angle of latitude. It is maximum at the poles and is absent at the equator.

The Coriolis force acts perpendicular to the pressure gradient force. The pressure gradient force is perpendicular to an isobar. The higher the pressure gradient force, the greater the velocity of the wind and the larger the deflection in the direction of wind. As a result of these two forces operating perpendicular to each other, in low-pressure areas the wind blows around it. At the equator, the Coriolis force is zero and the wind blows perpendicular to the isobars. The low pressure gets filled instead of getting intensified. That is the reason why tropical cyclones are not formed near the equator. Hence, both statements 1 and 2 are correct.

stem: One of the following regions has the world's largest tropical peatland, which holds about three years worth of global carbon emissions from fossil fuels; and the possible destruction of which can exert detrimental effect on the global climate. Which one of the following denotes that region?

runs: As per the article “Critical Ecosystems: Congo Basin Peatlands” published on the UNEP website in February, 2023, the Congo Basin is home to the world’s largest tropical peatlands, along with Brazil and Indonesia. The peat swamp forest of the Congo Basin stores around 29 billion tonnes of carbon - approximately equivalent to three years’ worth of global greenhouse gas emissions - while the Basin as a whole absorbs nearly 1.5 billion tonnes of carbon dioxide a year. Peatlands are an effective carbon sink - they absorb more carbon from the atmosphere than they produce. Carbon sinks are essential to combating the climate crisis and protecting planetary health. However, peatlands and other carbon sinks are already at risk of collapse due to climate change, nature and biodiversity loss, and pollution and waste. Without the critical services these ecosystems provide, the climate and nature crisis will only worsen.

stem: The ‘hydrological cycle’ is controlled by:

runs: Forests act as “water engineers” due to their leaf-rich canopy. They enable rainfall interception, high transpiration, pump-up of soil water by deep roots, and enhancement of water-holding capacity in carbon-rich soil layers, thereby facilitating groundwater recharge.
FAO’s Forests and Water
report also clarifies that forest canopies and litter layers regulate major hydrological processes such as rainfall interception, soil-water storage, and groundwater recharge.
Thus, forests are considered the most effective natural regulators of the hydrological cycle, while the impact of other options is local or limited.

Earth is tilted on its axis. If Earth had not been tilted on its axis, then days and nights would have been equal everywhere. In the same way, if Earth had not been revolving around the sun, then there would always have been longer days and shorter nights in one hemisphere and longer nights and shorter days in the other hemisphere. But except the equatorial line, the difference in the length of days and nights is seen in different seasons. On the equatorial line, days and nights are always equal.

runs: The Mediterranean climate has been developed between 30°- 40° latitudes in both hemispheres. The Mediterranean type of climate is characterized by dry summers and wet winters. The basic cause of this type of climate is the shifting of pressure and wind belts.

In summer, when Sun is overhead at Tropic of Cancer, the Westerlies belt is shifted poleward. The prevailing Trade winds are off-shore (terrestrial) and there is 'no rain'. The Mediterranean lands receive most of their precipitation in winter when the westerlies shift equatorward. The westerlies are associated with temperate cyclones and blow from sea surfaces, hence being moist yields sufficient rainfall in coastal areas.

stem: Consider the following statements with reference to Mediterranean climate:

runs: 1. It receives rainfall in winter season.
2. Due to winter solstice, air pressure belts shift to the South.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?

The Mediterranean climate generally develops between 30° and 40° Latitudes in both hemispheres, primarily on the western sides of continents. A key characteristic of the Mediterranean climate is that rainfall occurs in winter, while summers are usually dry.

The development of the Mediterranean climate occurs due to the shifting of pressure and wind belts caused by the northward and southward movement of the sun (Uttarayan and Dakshinayan) During winter (in the Northern Hemisphere), at the time of the winter solstice when sun is over the Tropic of Capricon, the westerly winds originating over the ocean expand into these northern latitudes. Since these mositure wind are associated with temperate cyclones, they cause rainfall.

During winter (in the contexst of the Southern Hemisphere), at the time of the summer solstice when the sun is over the tropic of cancer, the expansion of westerly winds originating over the oceans into these latitude bring winter rainfall. Note: Statement (2) is technically incorrect. It is only valid for the mediterranean climate in the Northern Hemisphere. The development of the mediterranean climate is not solely due to the southward shift of pressure belts during the winter solstice but also due to the northward shift to Pressure belts during the summer solstice (which corresponds to winter in the southern Hemisphere).

stem: With reference to the “EL-NINO”, which of the following statement/s is/are correct?
